   293	\paragraph{Direct index sampling (candidate direction, recommended).}
   294	Define, for arbitrary $m' \ge 1$, the line-point distribution over
   295	$\F_q^{m'}$ that samples the uniform point, the uniform axis index
   296	$i \in \{1,\ldots,m'\}$, and the diagonal direction with vanishing first
   297	$i-1$ coordinates, directly; define the \emph{directly indexed game} with
   298	this question distribution, whose line questions carry the index $i$ (and,
   299	for diagonal lines, the projected direction) in place of the seed
   300	$s \in \F_q$; and state the imported soundness theorem for that game
   301	(form~4 above).  This removes the divisibility obstruction and nothing
   302	else: the directly indexed game still asks for polynomials on revealed
   303	lines, has no pair questions, and weighs its branches as the present game
   304	does, so establishing form~4 carries the same two import obligations as
   305	the $\chi$-based import (Section~\ref{sec:import-obligations}), now at
   306	arbitrary dimension.
   307	
   308	The relation to the present game when $m' \mid q$ must moreover be proved
   309	at the level of games, not merely of question distributions, because the
   310	two games have different question alphabets: an $\mathsf{ALine}$ question
   311	of the $\chi$-based game is a pair $(u_0, s)$ and a $\mathsf{DLine}$
   312	question a triple $(u_0, s, v')$, so a strategy may select different
   313	measurements for seeds $s \ne s'$ with $\chi(s) = \chi(s')$, and equality
   314	of the induced laws of the geometric data does not by itself transport
   315	such a strategy.  The transport layer decomposes into the following
   316	obligations, none of which is carried out here.
   317	\begin{itemize}
   318	  \item \emph{Distribution lemma.}  When $m' \mid q$, the image of the
   319	  conditionally linear question distribution under the parsing map
   320	  $(u_0,s) \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s))$, $(u_0,s,v') \mapsto (u_0,\chi(s),v')$
   321	  is the direct distribution, and conditioned on the parsed question the
   322	  seed is uniform on the class $\chi^{-1}(i)$, independently of everything
   323	  else.
   324	  \item \emph{Parsing pullback.}  A strategy for the directly indexed game
   325	  composed with the parsing map is a seed-oblivious strategy for the
   326	  $\chi$-based game.  Since the win predicate depends on the question only
   327	  through the parsed data, and a seed-oblivious strategy answers
   328	  identically across each fiber --- in particular on the synchronicity
   329	  branches, where both players hold the same seed --- the value should be
   330	  preserved exactly on every branch, and projectivity is preserved.  This
   331	  is the direction the combining subtree needs.
   332	  \item \emph{Seed-fiber averaging: what it preserves and what it does
   333	  not.}  In the opposite direction, average each line measurement over its
   334	  seed fiber: attach to a direct question $(u_0,i)$, respectively
   335	  $(u_0,i,v')$, the average over uniform $s \in \chi^{-1}(i)$ of the
   336	  measurements attached to $(u_0,s)$, respectively $(u_0,s,v')$, leaving
   337	  the points measurements unchanged.  By the conditional uniformity of the
   338	  seed this preserves the value of every \emph{line-versus-point} branch
   339	  exactly: there the paired question carries no seed, so the branch value
   340	  is an average over the fiber of per-seed values, which the averaged
   341	  measurement computes.  It does \emph{not} preserve the synchronicity
   342	  branches.  There both players hold the same seed, so the $\chi$-based
   343	  branch value is the diagonal average
   344	  $\E_{s}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s)}_f
   345	  \rangle$, while the averaged strategy realizes the double average
   346	  $\E_{s,s'}\sum_f \langle M^{(u_0,s)}_f \ot \widetilde M^{(u_0,s')}_f
   347	  \rangle$ over independent seeds in the fiber; the two differ whenever
   348	  the players' measurements vary across a fiber in a correlated way (if
   349	  both apply a common seed-dependent relabelling, every diagonal term is
   350	  large and the cross terms are not), and neither quantity dominates the
   351	  other in general.  An earlier revision of this note claimed that the
   352	  averaging preserves the exact value, and with it synchronicity; that
   353	  claim was wrong and is withdrawn.  What needs proof is control of the
   354	  synchronicity branches under de-seeding.  Candidate approaches: show
   355	  that a strategy of value $1-\eps$ in the $\chi$-based game is, with
   356	  polynomial loss, close to a seed-oblivious one; or state form~4 with a
   357	  synchronicity hypothesis in the doubled-average form and re-derive it on
   358	  the tensor-code side.  Choosing and proving one of these is an open
   359	  obligation.
   360	  \item \emph{Projectivity round trip.}  The averaged strategy is a POVM
   361	  strategy even when the given one is projective, while the imported
   362	  theorem, like the present one, takes projective strategies.  The
   363	  intended round trip is: dilate the averaged strategy to a projective one
   364	  (Naimark preserves all product correlations
   365	  $\langle X \ot Y \rangle$ of the given strategy against the dilated
   366	  state --- hence the value of every branch the averaging preserved ---
   367	  but nothing restores the diagonal seed correlations once the averaging
   368	  has been performed); apply form~4; and compress the resulting polynomial
   369	  measurement along the dilation isometry back to a POVM in the required
   370	  measurement class on the original space.  That this compression
   371	  preserves the consistency conclusions must itself be proved; it is
   372	  stated here as an obligation, not established.  (Alternatively, form~4
   373	  may be stated for POVM strategies outright, moving the dilation inside
   374	  the import.)
   375	\end{itemize}

   149	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   150	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   151	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   152	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   153	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   154	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

   156	/-- Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree
   157	test (`lem:ld-soundness`, blueprint lines 135--160; paper theorem and proof

   172	          ∃ GA : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιA, ∃ GB : PolyMeasTuple L S.ιB,

   178	                (fun u outcome =>

   183	                (fun u outcome =>
   184	                  heteroKron
   185	                    ((GA.postprocess (evalPolyTupleAt u)).effect outcome) 1)
   186	                (fun u outcome =>
   187	                  heteroKron 1
   188	                    (((S.B (ldPointQuestionOf L u)).postprocess
   189	                      (ldPointValuesOrZero L)).effect outcome))

   191	            consistencyDefect (uniformDistribution Unit)
   192	                (fun _ g => heteroKron (GA.effect g) 1)
   193	                (fun _ g => heteroKron 1 (GB.effect g))

     4	/-!
     5	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     6	
     7	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
     8	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
     9	`Measurement` structure.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    14	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	/--
    27	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    28	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    31	-/
    32	structure Game where
    33	  QuestionA : Type
    34	  QuestionB : Type
    35	  AnswerA : Type
    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    38	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    39	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    41	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    42	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    43	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    44	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    45	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    46	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    48	
    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    75	
    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152	
   153	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	/-! # Strategy classes and symmetric games
     6	
     7	This module defines projective, commuting, consistent, PCC, and SPCC strategy
     8	predicates from `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:89-183`, with source
     9	definitions in `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-180`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    13	
    14	universe u
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    17	
    18	/-- Projectivity from `def:projective-strategy-general`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:90-101`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`. -/
    20	def Strategy.IsProjective {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : Prop :=
    21	  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.A x)) ∧
    22	    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.B y)
    23	
    24	/-- Symmetric games from `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    25	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`.
    26	The question and answer alphabets are each represented by a single shared type,
    27	matching the source notation. -/
    28	structure SymmetricGame where
    29	  Question : Type
    30	  Answer : Type
    31	  [questionFintype : Fintype Question]
    32	  [answerFintype : Fintype Answer]
    33	  [questionDecidableEq : DecidableEq Question]
    34	  [answerDecidableEq : DecidableEq Answer]
    35	  μ : Distribution (Question × Question)
    36	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    37	  μ_symm : ∀ x y, μ.weight (x, y) = μ.weight (y, x)
    38	  decide : Question → Question → Answer → Answer → Bool
    39	  decide_symm : ∀ x y a b, decide x y a b = decide y x b a
    40	
    41	attribute [instance] SymmetricGame.questionFintype SymmetricGame.answerFintype
    42	  SymmetricGame.questionDecidableEq SymmetricGame.answerDecidableEq
    43	
    44	/-- Regard a symmetric game as a game with equal question and answer types;
    45	`def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    46	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
    47	def SymmetricGame.toGame (G : SymmetricGame) : Game where
    48	  QuestionA := G.Question
    49	  QuestionB := G.Question
    50	  AnswerA := G.Answer
    51	  AnswerB := G.Answer
    52	  μ := G.μ
    53	  μ_prob := G.μ_prob
    54	  decide := G.decide
    55	
    56	/-- Symmetric strategies from `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    57	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`.
    58	The two local spaces and measurement families are identified, as in the source
    59	definition. -/
    60	structure SymmetricStrategy (G : SymmetricGame) where
    61	  ι : Type
    62	  [ιFintype : Fintype ι]
    63	  [ιDecidableEq : DecidableEq ι]
    64	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)
    65	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    66	  ψ_swap : reindexState (Equiv.prodComm ι ι) ψ = ψ
    67	  M : G.Question → Measurement G.Answer ι
    68	
    69	attribute [instance] SymmetricStrategy.ιFintype SymmetricStrategy.ιDecidableEq
    70	
    71	/-- Regard a symmetric strategy as a strategy using the same local space and
    72	measurement family for both players; `def:symmetric-game`, blueprint
    73	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:100-109`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:74-92`. -/
    74	def SymmetricStrategy.toStrategy {G : SymmetricGame} (S : SymmetricStrategy G) :
    75	    Strategy G.toGame where
    76	  ιA := S.ι
    77	  ιB := S.ι
    78	  ψ := S.ψ
    79	  ψ_norm := S.ψ_norm
    80	  A := S.M
    81	  B := S.M
    82	
    83	/-- Common-space commutation from `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
    84	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:141-150`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
    85	def IsCommutingOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
    86	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
    87	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β]
    88	    [DecidableEq β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    89	    (μ : Distribution (X × Y)) (A : X → Measurement α ι)
    90	    (B : Y → Measurement β ι) : Prop :=
    91	  ∀ x y, 0 < μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b, Commute ((A x).effect a) ((B y).effect b)
    92	
    93	private def transportOp {d₁ d₂ : Type u} (h : d₁ = d₂) (M : Op d₂) : Op d₁ :=
    94	  h.symm ▸ M
    95	
    96	/-- Transported common-space form of `def:comm-strategy`, blueprint
    97	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:141-150`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:132-142`. -/
    98	def Strategy.IsCommuting {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) (hι : S.ιA = S.ιB) : Prop :=
    99	  ∀ x y, 0 < G.μ.weight (x, y) → ∀ a b,
   100	    Commute ((S.A x).effect a) (transportOp hι ((S.B y).effect b))
   101	
   102	/-- Measurement consistency from `def:consistent-measurement`, blueprint
   103	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:152-161`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:144-160`. -/
   104	def Measurement.IsConsistentOn {α ι : Type*}
   105	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   106	    (M : Measurement α ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
   107	  ∀ a, (heteroKron (M.effect a) 1).mulVec ψ =
   108	    (heteroKron 1 (M.effect a)).mulVec ψ
   109	
   110	/-- General strategy consistency from `def:consistent-strategy`, blueprint
   111	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:169-174`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
   112	def IsConsistentStrategyOn {X Y α β ι : Type*}
   113	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype Y] [DecidableEq Y]
   114	    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β]
   115	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   116	    (A : X → Measurement α ι) (B : Y → Measurement β ι)
   117	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
   118	  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (A x) ψ) ∧
   119	    ∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (B y) ψ
   120	
   121	/-- Symmetric strategy consistency from `def:consistent-strategy`, blueprint
   122	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:169-174`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:162-174`. -/
   123	def SymmetricStrategy.IsConsistent {G : SymmetricGame}
   124	    (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
   125	  ∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn (S.M x) S.ψ
   126	
   127	/-- The PCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:178-183`,
   128	paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:176-180`. -/
   129	def Strategy.IsPCC {G : Game} {ι : Type*}
   130	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   131	    (μ : Distribution (G.QuestionA × G.QuestionB))
   132	    (A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ι)
   133	    (B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ι)
   134	  (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
   135	  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (A x)) ∧
   136	    (∀ y, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (B y)) ∧
   137	    IsConsistentStrategyOn A B ψ ∧ IsCommutingOn μ A B
   138	
   139	/-- The SPCC predicate `def:spcc`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:178-183`,
   140	paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:176-180`. -/
   141	def SymmetricStrategy.IsSPCC {G : SymmetricGame}
   142	  (S : SymmetricStrategy G) : Prop :=
   143	  (∀ x, MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.M x)) ∧ S.IsConsistent ∧
   144	    IsCommutingOn G.μ S.M S.M
   145	
   146	/-- Source symmetrization statement `lem:symmetric-strat`, blueprint
   147	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:116-135`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-130`.
   148	The attainment defect is `rem:symmetric-strat-limit` and is tracked in
   149	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_symmetrization-attainment.tex`. -/
   150	theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy (G : SymmetricGame) (ε : ℝ)
   151	    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (h : G.toGame.value = 1 - ε) :
   152	    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
   153	      1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
   154	  sorry
   155	
   156	/-- Value-preserving formalization-only form of `lem:symmetric-strat` starting
   157	from a specified near-optimal strategy; blueprint
   158	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:116-135`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:94-130`.
   159	The source attainment distinction is tracked in
   160	`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_symmetrization-attainment.tex`. -/
   161	theorem exists_symmetric_projective_strategy_of_strategy (G : SymmetricGame)
   162	    (ε : ℝ) (S₀ : Strategy G.toGame) (h : 1 - ε ≤ S₀.value) :
   163	    ∃ S : SymmetricStrategy G, S.toStrategy.IsProjective ∧
   164	      S.toStrategy.value = S₀.value ∧ 1 - ε ≤ S.toStrategy.value := by
   165	  sorry
   166	
   167	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    18	/-- Evaluate a polynomial-valued submeasurement at a point. -/
    19	noncomputable def evaluateAt {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    20	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] (u : Point params)
    21	    (G : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι) : SubMeas (Fq params) ι :=
    22	  postprocess G (fun g => g u)

    24	/-- Evaluation after adjoining an unused coordinate agrees with evaluation before
    25	adjoining that coordinate. -/
    26	@[simp] theorem evaluateAt_postprocess_appendAtHeight_appendPoint
    27	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    28	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    29	    (G : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι)
    30	    (x : Fq params) (u : Point params) (y : Fq params) :
    31	    evaluateAt params.next (appendPoint params u y)
    32	        (postprocess G (fun g => Polynomial.appendAtHeight params g x)) =
    33	      evaluateAt params u G := by
    34	  unfold evaluateAt
    35	  rw [SubMeas.postprocess_comp]
    36	  congr
    37	  funext g
    38	  exact Polynomial.appendAtHeight_apply_appendPoint params g x u y

    40	/-- View a global polynomial submeasurement as a point-indexed answer family. -/

    42	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    43	    (G : SubMeas (Polynomial params) ι) :
    44	    IdxSubMeas (Point params) (Fq params) ι :=
    45	  fun u => evaluateAt params u G

    48	
    49	The submeasurement-valued `polynomialEvaluationFamily` is the form used by most

    84	/-- Questionwise matching mass `∑_a ⟨ψ, A_a B_a ψ⟩`, summed over outcomes. -/
    85	noncomputable def qMatchMass {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    86	    [Fintype Outcome]
    87	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
    88	  ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a * B.outcome a)
    89	
    90	/-- Questionwise off-diagonal mass surrogate for consistency. -/
    91	noncomputable def qConsDefect {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    92	    [Fintype Outcome]
    93	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
    94	  let totalOverlap := ev ψ (A.total * B.total)
    95	  max 0 (totalOverlap - qMatchMass ψ A B)
    96	
    97	/-- Questionwise squared-distance defect. -/
    98	noncomputable def qSDDCore {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    99	    [Fintype Outcome]
   100	    (ψ : QuantumState ι)
   101	    (A B : Outcome → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) : Error :=
   102	  ∑ a, ev ψ ((A a - B a)ᴴ * (A a - B a))
   103	
   104	/-- Questionwise squared-distance defect. -/
   105	noncomputable def qSDD {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   106	    [Fintype Outcome]
   107	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
   108	  qSDDCore ψ A.outcome B.outcome

   110	/-- State-dependent distance for raw operator families.
   111	Matches the paper's `≈_δ` for arbitrary matrix families.
   112	This keeps the raw-family API separate while sharing the same core formula as
   113	`qSDD`. -/
   114	noncomputable def qSDDOp {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   115	    [Fintype Outcome]
   116	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A B : OpFamily Outcome ι) : Error :=
   117	  qSDDCore ψ A.outcome B.outcome
   118	
   119	/-- Questionwise strong self-consistency defect. -/
   120	noncomputable def qSSCDefect {Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   121	    [Fintype Outcome]
   122	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (A : SubMeas Outcome ι) : Error :=
   123	  let totalMass := ev ψ A.total
   124	  let diagonalMass := ∑ a, ev ψ (A.outcome a * A.outcome a)
   125	  max 0 (totalMass - diagonalMass)

   127	/-- Averaged off-diagonal mass for consistency statements. -/
   128	noncomputable def consError {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   129	    [Fintype Outcome]
   130	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   131	    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : Error :=
   132	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qConsDefect ψ (A q) (B q))
   133	
   134	/-- Averaged squared distance for `≈_δ`. -/
   135	noncomputable def sddError {Question Outcome : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   136	    [Fintype Outcome]
   137	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (𝒟 : Distribution Question)
   138	    (A B : IdxSubMeas Question Outcome ι) : Error :=
   139	  avgOver 𝒟 (fun q => qSDD ψ (A q) (B q))

     6	/-!
     7	# The low-degree game
     8	
     9	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    10	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    11	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    12	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    17	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient
    31	space uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a
    32	model supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for
    33	`def:ld-game` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    36	-/
    37	structure LdParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  k : ℕ
    42	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    43	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    44	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    45	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    46	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    47	
    48	/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type
    49	used by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/
    50	instance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=
    51	  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩
    52	
    53	/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility
    54	view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified
    55	parameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    57	-/
    58	noncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    59	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq
    60	
    61	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    62	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.
    63	Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    65	-/
    66	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K
    67	
    68	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    71	-/
    72	inductive LdType where
    73	  | point
    74	  | aline
    75	  | dline
    76	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    77	
    78	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    79	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    80	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    81	-/
    82	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    83	
    84	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    85	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
    87	-/
    88	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    89	
    90	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    91	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    92	-/
    93	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    94	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    95	
    96	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    97	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    98	-/
    99	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
   100	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
   101	
   102	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   104	-/
   105	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   106	  fun i => z (.inr i)
   107	
   108	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   109	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   110	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   114	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   115	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   116	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   117	
   118	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   119	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   120	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   121	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   122	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   123	-/
   124	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   125	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   126	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   127	
   128	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   129	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   130	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   131	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   132	-/
   133	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   134	  fun i => match i with
   135	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   136	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   137	  | .inr _ => 0
   138	
   139	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   140	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   141	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   142	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   143	-/
   144	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   145	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   146	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   147	  fun i => match i with
   148	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   149	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   150	  | .inr _ => 0
   151	
   152	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   153	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   154	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   155	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   156	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   157	-/
   158	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   159	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   160	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   161	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   162	  fun i => match i with
   163	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   164	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   165	  | .inr j => direction j
   166	
   167	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   168	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   169	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   170	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   171	-/
   172	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   173	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   174	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   175	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P

   195	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   196	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   197	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   199	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   200	
   201	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   202	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   203	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   204	-/
   205	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   206	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   207	  Distribution.map
   208	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   209	    (fun s =>

   211

   213	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   214	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint

   222	  deriving DecidableEq
   223	
   224	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   225	instance; the public constructors are those of `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   226	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   227	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   228	-/
   229	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   230	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   231	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   232	      (Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P))
   233	
   234	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `LdAnswer` (Lean-only
   235	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   236	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   237	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   238	-/
   239	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   240	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where
   241	  toFun
   242	    | .pointVals a => .inl a
   243	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   244	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)
   245	  invFun
   246	    | .inl a => .pointVals a
   247	    | .inr (.inl a) => .alinePolys a
   248	    | .inr (.inr a) => .dlinePolys a
   249	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
   250	  right_inv := by
   251	    intro x
   252	    cases x with
   253	    | inl a => rfl
   254	    | inr x =>
   255	        cases x with
   256	        | inl a => rfl
   257	        | inr a => rfl
   258	
   259	instance (P : LdParams) : Inhabited (LdAnswer P) :=
   260	  ⟨.pointVals (fun _ => 0)⟩
   261	
   262	noncomputable instance (P : LdParams) : Fintype (LdAnswer P) :=
   263	  Fintype.ofEquiv (LdAnswerCode P) (ldAnswerEquiv P).symm
   264	
   265	/-- Evaluation of a coefficient tuple at a field element.  This is the
   266	representative convention used by the line answers in `def:ld-win-predicate`,
   267	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   268	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   269	-/
   270	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}
   271	    (c : Fin n → K) (t : K) : K :=
   272	  ∑ i : Fin n, c i * t ^ i.val
   273	
   274	/-- Check that an answer has the constructor prescribed by its question type;
   275	Lean encoding of the rejection clause in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   276	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   277	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   278	-/
   279	def validLdAnswer {P : LdParams} (t : LdType) (a : LdAnswer P) : Bool :=
   280	  match t, a with
   281	  | .point, .pointVals _ => true
   282	  | .aline, .alinePolys _ => true
   283	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   284	  | _, _ => false
   285	
   286	/-- The axis-parallel line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   287	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   288	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   289	-/
   290	def alinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   291	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   292	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   293	  -- Universal quantification follows the zero-direction convention in
   294	  -- `rem:ld-win-zero-direction`.
   295	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   296	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   297	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   298	
   299	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   300	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   301	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   302	-/
   303	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   304	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   305	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   306	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   307	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   308	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j
   309	
   310	/-- The low-degree consistency predicate, rejecting answers of the wrong
   311	constructor shape.  This is `def:ld-win-predicate` in
   312	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:56-105`, paper origin
   313	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   314	-/
   315	noncomputable def ldWinPredicate (P : LdParams) :
   316	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=
   317	  open Classical in
   318	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   319	      if validLdAnswer tA a && validLdAnswer tB b then
   320	        match tA, tB, a, b with
   321	        | .point, .point, .pointVals u, .pointVals v => decide (u = v)
   322	        | .aline, .point, .alinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   323	            decide (alinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   324	        | .point, .aline, .pointVals u, .alinePolys f =>
   325	            decide (alinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   326	        | .dline, .point, .dlinePolys f, .pointVals u =>
   327	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xA xB f u)
   328	        | .point, .dline, .pointVals u, .dlinePolys f =>
   329	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   330	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   331	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   332	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   333	      else false
   334	
   335	/-- The low-degree game packaged as a `Game`.  This is `def:ld-game` in
   336	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, paper origin
   337	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   338	-/
   339	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where
   340	  QuestionA := LdQuestion P
   341	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   342	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   343	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   344	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   345	  μ_prob := by sorry
   346	  decide := ldWinPredicate P
   347	
   348	end
   349	
   350	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    32	/-- Parameters for the `(m,q,d)` low individual degree test.
    33	
    34	Besides the usual positivity assumptions, we bundle the paper-faithful witness
    35	that `q = p^n` is a prime power. -/
    36	structure Parameters where
    37	  m : ℕ
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  d : ℕ
    40	  hm : 0 < m
    41	  /-- Kept as a compatibility field so existing positivity proofs can continue
    42	  to use `params.hq`; it is derivable from `hqPrimePower`. -/
    43	  hq : 0 < q
    44	  /-- Paper-faithful witness that `q` is a prime power. -/
    45	  hqPrimePower : ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n
    46	
    47	deriving instance DecidableEq for Parameters

    49	namespace Parameters
    50	
    51	/-- Any number presented as a prime power is automatically positive. -/
    52	theorem q_pos_of_primePower {q : ℕ}
    53	    (hqPrimePower : ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n) : 0 < q := by
    54	  rcases hqPrimePower with ⟨p, n, hp, hn, rfl⟩
    55	  exact Nat.pow_pos hp.pos
    56	
    57	/-- Prime numbers are prime powers of exponent `1`. -/
    58	theorem prime_primePower {q : ℕ} (hqPrime : Nat.Prime q) :
    59	    ∃ p n, Nat.Prime p ∧ 0 < n ∧ q = p ^ n := by
    60	  exact ⟨q, 1, hqPrime, by decide, by simp⟩
    61	
    62	/-- Build parameters from explicit prime-power data `q = p^n`. -/
    63	def ofPrimePower (m q d p n : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hn : 0 < n)
    64	    (hq : q = p ^ n) : Parameters :=
    65	  { m := m
    66	    q := q
    67	    d := d
    68	    hm := hm
    69	    hq := q_pos_of_primePower ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩
    70	    hqPrimePower := ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩ }
    71	
    72	/-- Build parameters when `q` itself is prime. -/
    73	def ofPrime (m q d : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) (hqPrime : Nat.Prime q) : Parameters :=
    74	  { m := m
    75	    q := q
    76	    d := d
    77	    hm := hm
    78	    hq := hqPrime.pos
    79	    hqPrimePower := prime_primePower hqPrime }

    81	/-- Convenience constructor for the ubiquitous binary field. -/
    82	def ofTwo (m d : ℕ) (hm : 0 < m) : Parameters :=

    85	/-- Paper finite fields have at least two elements: `q = p^n` with `p` prime

    87	theorem two_le_q (params : Parameters) : 2 ≤ params.q := by
    88	  obtain ⟨p, n, hp, hn, hq⟩ := params.hqPrimePower
    89	  rw [hq]
    90	  exact le_trans hp.two_le (Nat.le_self_pow (Nat.ne_of_gt hn) p)
    91	
    92	/-- The field-size parameter is strictly larger than `1`. -/
    93	theorem one_lt_q (params : Parameters) : 1 < params.q :=

    95	
    96	/-- Positivity of the field-size parameter after casting to the repository's
    97	real-valued error scalar type. -/
    98	theorem q_cast_pos (params : Parameters) : 0 < (params.q : Error) :=

   106	/-- The successor test obtained by appending one coordinate. -/
   107	def Parameters.next (params : Parameters) : Parameters :=

   109	    q := params.q
   110	    d := params.d
   111	    hm := Nat.succ_pos _

   116	
   117	/-- The predecessor parameters obtained by removing the last coordinate from a
   118	non-base ambient dimension.
   119	
   120	This is the inverse construction to `Parameters.next` on the data fields.  The
   121	proof fields are inherited from the original parameter bundle, so the inverse is
   122	propositional rather than definitional. -/
   123	def previous (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) : Parameters :=
   124	  { m := params.m - 1
   125	    q := params.q
   126	    d := params.d
   127	    hm := Nat.sub_pos_of_lt hm
   128	    hq := params.hq
   129	    hqPrimePower := params.hqPrimePower }
   130	
   131	/-- Removing the last coordinate and then applying `Parameters.next` recovers the
   132	original non-base parameters. -/
   133	theorem previous_next_eq (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
   134	    (previous params hm).next = params := by
   135	  cases params with
   136	  | mk m q d hm0 hq hqPrimePower =>
   137	      have hsub : m - 1 + 1 = m := Nat.sub_add_cancel (le_of_lt hm)
   138	      simp [previous, Parameters.next, hsub]
   139	
   140	/-- A bundled predecessor for a parameter set known to be a successor dimension. -/
   141	structure SuccessorDecomposition (params : Parameters) where
   142	  /-- The predecessor parameter bundle. -/
   143	  pred : Parameters
   144	  /-- The predecessor's successor is the original parameter bundle. -/
   145	  next_eq : pred.next = params
   146	
   147	/-- Every parameter bundle of dimension strictly larger than one has a bundled
   148	predecessor whose successor is propositionally equal to the original bundle. -/
   149	def successorDecompositionOfOneLtM (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
   150	    SuccessorDecomposition params where
   151	  pred := previous params hm
   152	  next_eq := previous_next_eq params hm
   153	
   154	/-- A positive dimension that is not the base dimension is strictly larger than
   155	one. -/
   156	theorem one_lt_m_of_ne_one (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :

   160	/-- Non-base parameters have a bundled predecessor decomposition. -/
   161	def successorDecompositionOfNeOne (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :
   162	    SuccessorDecomposition params :=
   163	  successorDecompositionOfOneLtM params (one_lt_m_of_ne_one params hm_ne_one)
   164	
   165	end Parameters

   210	/-- A bundled field model for the paper's `F_q`, together with a coding equivalence
   211	to the repository's finite carrier `Fin q`. -/
   212	class FieldModel (q : ℕ) where

   214	  instField : Field K
   215	  instFintype : Fintype K
   216	  instDecidableEq : DecidableEq K

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-field bases and the fixed binary representation
     5	
     6	The Pauli basis test uses fields of size `2^k` for odd `k`, together with a
     7	chosen self-dual normal basis over `ZMod 2`.  This file constructs such bases
     8	and records the resulting fixed field model for later proofs.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The declarations correspond to `def:admissible-size`,
    13	`def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, `def:subfields-kappa`, `def:subfield-trace`,
    14	and `def:binary-representation` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:182-257` and `298-315`.
    16	Their paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:433-502,653-728`.
