    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	/-- `IsAdmissibleSize q` is the predicate `q = 2^k` for an odd exponent.
    24	This is `def:admissible-size` in the blueprint
    25	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:210-212`, with paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:662-667`.
    27	-/
    28	def IsAdmissibleSize (q : ℕ) : Prop := ∃ k : ℕ, Odd k ∧ q = 2 ^ k
    29	
    30	/-- A dual pair of bases for `def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, blueprint
    31	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:241-257`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:494-496`. -/
    32	def IsDualBasisPair {F K ι : Type*} [CommRing F] [CommRing K] [DecidableEq ι]
    33	    [Algebra F K] (b b' : Module.Basis ι F K) : Prop :=
    34	  ∀ i j, Algebra.trace F K (b i * b' j) = if i = j then 1 else 0
    35	
    36	namespace Basis
    37	
    38	/-- Self-duality in `def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, blueprint
    39	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:241-257`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:494-497`. -/
    40	def IsSelfDual {F K ι : Type*} [CommRing F] [CommRing K] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    [Algebra F K] (b : Module.Basis ι F K) : Prop :=
    42	  IsDualBasisPair b b
    43	
    44	/-- Normality in `def:dual-self-dual-normal-basis`, blueprint
    45	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:241-257`, paper `04_preliminaries.tex:498-502`. The
    46	Frobenius exponent uses the cardinality of the base field. -/
    47	def IsNormal {F K : Type*} [CommSemiring F] [Fintype F] [Field K] [Algebra F K]
    48	    {k : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin k) F K) : Prop :=
    49	  ∃ α : K, ∀ j, b j = α ^ (Fintype.card F ^ j.1)
    50	
    51	end Basis
    52	
    53	/- The characteristic-two self-dual normal-basis construction is carried out
    54	in the group algebra of the finite Galois group.  The transition from a normal
    55	basis to its trace dual is a symmetric unit; odd cardinality makes its square
    56	root unique and symmetric. -/
    57	
    58	section GroupAlgebra
    59	
    60	variable {G : Type*} [CommGroup G]
    61	
    62	/-- The squaring automorphism of a commutative group whose `Nat.card` is odd. -/
    63	private noncomputable def squareMulEquiv (hodd : Odd (Nat.card G)) : G ≃* G :=
    64	  MulEquiv.ofBijective (powMonoidHom 2) hodd.coprime_two_right.pow_left_bijective
    65	
    66	private theorem monoid_algebra_sq_eq_dom_congr (hodd : Odd (Nat.card G))
    67	    (x : MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G) :
    68	    x ^ 2 = MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (squareMulEquiv hodd) x := by
    69	  letI : CharP (MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G) 2 :=
    70	    charP_of_injective_algebraMap' (ZMod 2) 2
    71	  induction x using MonoidAlgebra.induction_linear with
    72	  | zero => simp
    73	  | add x y hx hy =>
    74	      rw [add_pow_char, hx, hy, map_add]
    75	  | single g r =>
    76	      simp [MonoidAlgebra.single_pow, squareMulEquiv, ZMod.pow_card]
    77	
    78	private theorem monoid_algebra_sq_bijective (hodd : Odd (Nat.card G)) :
    79	    Function.Bijective (fun x : MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G => x ^ 2) := by
    80	  have heq : (fun x : MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G => x ^ 2) =
    81	      MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (squareMulEquiv hodd) := by
    82	    funext x
    83	    exact monoid_algebra_sq_eq_dom_congr hodd x
    84	  rw [heq]
    85	  exact (MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (squareMulEquiv hodd)).bijective
    86	
    87	end GroupAlgebra
    88	
    89	section NormalTraceDual
    90	
    91	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    92	
    93	local notation "G" => Gal(K/(ZMod 2))
    94	
    95	noncomputable local instance : CommGroup G := IsCyclic.commGroup
    96	noncomputable local instance : DecidableEq G := Classical.decEq G
    97	
    98	private theorem normal_basis_trace_dual_apply (σ : G) :
    99	    (IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).traceDual σ =
   100	      σ ((IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).traceDual 1) := by
   101	  classical
   102	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   103	  have hdual : (b.traceDual : G → K) = fun τ => τ (b.traceDual 1) := by
   104	    rw [b.traceDual_eq_iff]
   105	    intro τ υ
   106	    simp only [Algebra.traceForm_apply]
   107	    calc
   108	      Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (τ (b.traceDual 1) * b υ) =
   109	          Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K
   110	            (τ⁻¹ (τ (b.traceDual 1) * b υ)) := by
   111	              symm
   112	              exact Algebra.trace_eq_of_algEquiv τ⁻¹ _
   113	      _ = Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (b.traceDual 1 * b (τ⁻¹ * υ)) := by
   114	        congr 2
   115	        rw [map_mul]
   116	        have hτ : τ⁻¹ (τ (b.traceDual 1)) = b.traceDual 1 := by
   117	          change τ.symm (τ (b.traceDual 1)) = b.traceDual 1
   118	          exact τ.symm_apply_apply _
   119	        have hυ : τ⁻¹ (b υ) = b (τ⁻¹ * υ) := by
   120	          calc
   121	            τ⁻¹ (b υ) = τ⁻¹ (υ (b 1)) := by
   122	              rw [IsGalois.normalBasis_apply]
   123	            _ = (τ⁻¹ * υ) (b 1) := rfl
   124	            _ = b (τ⁻¹ * υ) := (IsGalois.normalBasis_apply _).symm
   125	        rw [hτ, hυ]
   126	      _ = if τ⁻¹ * υ = 1 then 1 else 0 := b.trace_traceDual_mul 1 (τ⁻¹ * υ)
   127	      _ = if υ = τ then 1 else 0 := by simp only [inv_mul_eq_one, eq_comm]
   128	  exact congr_fun hdual σ
   129	
   130	private theorem normal_basis_repr_symm_mul_single
   131	    (a : MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G) (σ : G) (r : ZMod 2) :
   132	    ((MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans
   133	        (IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).repr.symm)
   134	        (a * MonoidAlgebra.single σ r) =
   135	      r • σ (((MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans
   136	        (IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).repr.symm) a) := by
   137	  classical
   138	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   139	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   140	  change φ (a * MonoidAlgebra.single σ r) = r • σ (φ a)
   141	  induction a using MonoidAlgebra.induction_linear with
   142	  | zero => simp
   143	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [add_mul, map_add, hx, hy, smul_add]
   144	  | single τ s =>
   145	      simp only [MonoidAlgebra.single_mul_single, φ, LinearEquiv.trans_apply,
   146	        MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv_apply, MonoidAlgebra.coeff_single,
   147	        b.repr_symm_single, map_smul, smul_smul]
   148	      rw [mul_comm s r]
   149	      apply congrArg (fun x : K => (r * s) • x)
   150	      rw [mul_comm τ σ]
   151	      calc
   152	        b (σ * τ) = (σ * τ) (b 1) := IsGalois.normalBasis_apply _
   153	        _ = σ (τ (b 1)) := rfl
   154	        _ = σ (b τ) := congrArg σ (IsGalois.normalBasis_apply τ).symm
   155	
   156	private theorem normal_basis_transition (a : MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G) :
   157	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   158	    let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   159	    let ψ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.traceDual.repr.symm
   160	    let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   161	    φ (v * a) = ψ a := by
   162	  classical
   163	  dsimp only
   164	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   165	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   166	  let ψ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.traceDual.repr.symm
   167	  let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   168	  change φ (v * a) = ψ a
   169	  induction a using MonoidAlgebra.induction_linear with
   170	  | zero => simp
   171	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [mul_add, map_add, hx, hy]
   172	  | single σ r =>
   173	      rw [normal_basis_repr_symm_mul_single]
   174	      rw [show φ v = b.traceDual 1 from φ.apply_symm_apply _]
   175	      simp only [ψ, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv_apply,
   176	        MonoidAlgebra.coeff_single, b.traceDual.repr_symm_single]
   177	      exact congrArg (fun x : K => r • x) (normal_basis_trace_dual_apply σ).symm
   178	
   179	private theorem normal_basis_transition_is_unit :
   180	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   181	    let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   182	    IsUnit (φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)) := by
   183	  classical
   184	  dsimp only
   185	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   186	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   187	  let ψ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.traceDual.repr.symm
   188	  let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   189	  change IsUnit v
   190	  rw [IsUnit.isUnit_iff_mulLeft_bijective]
   191	  have heq : (fun a => v * a) = fun a => φ.symm (ψ a) := by
   192	    funext a
   193	    apply φ.injective
   194	    rw [φ.apply_symm_apply]
   195	    exact normal_basis_transition a
   196	  rw [heq]
   197	  exact φ.symm.bijective.comp ψ.bijective
   198	
   199	private theorem normal_basis_repr_apply_eq_trace (x : K) (σ : G) :
   200	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   201	    (b.repr x) σ = Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (x * b.traceDual σ) := by
   202	  classical
   203	  dsimp only
   204	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   205	  simpa only [Algebra.traceForm_apply, b.traceDual_traceDual] using
   206	    b.traceDual.traceDual_repr_apply x σ
   207	
   208	private theorem normal_basis_transition_inv :
   209	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   210	    let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   211	    let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   212	    MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (MulEquiv.inv G) v = v := by
   213	  classical
   214	  dsimp only
   215	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   216	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   217	  let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   218	  let invAlg := MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (MulEquiv.inv G)
   219	  change invAlg v = v
   220	  ext σ

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.ParametersBase
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Axis-parallel lines for the low individual degree test
     5	
     6	Axis-parallel line geometry on top of the core parameter infrastructure:
     7	`AxisParallelLine` records a base point and a coordinate direction, with
     8	canonical parameterization, rebasing, and slice-embedding operations.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex`
    13	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch02_test.tex`
    14	-/
    15	
    16	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    17	
    18	/-- A genuinely axis-parallel affine line in `F_q^m`. -/
    19	structure AxisParallelLine (params : Parameters) where
    20	  base : Point params
    21	  direction : Fin params.m
    22	
    23	deriving instance DecidableEq, Inhabited for AxisParallelLine
    24	
    25	namespace AxisParallelLine
    26	
    27	/-- The canonical affine parameterization `t ↦ base + t e_i`. -/
    28	def pointAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    29	    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) : Fq params → Point params :=
    30	  fun t i =>
    31	    if i = ℓ.direction then
    32	      addCoord (ℓ.base i) t
    33	    else
    34	      ℓ.base i
    35	
    36	/-- Canonical geometric axis-parallel line through `u` in direction `i`.
    37	
    38	The representative stores zero in the moving coordinate, so all points on the
    39	same geometric line map to the same `AxisParallelLine`. -/
    40	def throughPoint {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    41	    (u : Point params) (i : Fin params.m) : AxisParallelLine params where
    42	  base := fun j => if j = i then zeroCoord else u j
    43	  direction := i
    44	
    45	/-- Affine parameter of the sampled point on the canonical axis-parallel line
    46	through `u` in direction `i`. -/
    47	def sampleParameter {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    48	    (u : Point params) (i : Fin params.m) : Fq params :=
    49	  u i
    50	
    51	/-- Rebase an axis-parallel line so that the old point `ℓ.pointAt t`
    52	becomes the new base point. -/
    53	def rebaseAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    54	    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (t : Fq params) : AxisParallelLine params where
    55	  base := ℓ.pointAt t
    56	  direction := ℓ.direction
    57	
    58	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_pointAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    59	    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (t : Fq params) :
    60	    (rebaseAt ℓ t).pointAt zeroCoord = ℓ.pointAt t := by
    61	  ext i
    62	  simp [rebaseAt, pointAt, addCoord, zeroCoord]
    63	
    64	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    65	    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) :
    66	    rebaseAt ℓ zeroCoord = ℓ := by
    67	  cases ℓ with
    68	  | mk base direction =>
    69	      change
    70	        ({ base :=
    71	             ({ base := base, direction := direction } : AxisParallelLine params).pointAt zeroCoord,
    72	           direction := direction } : AxisParallelLine params) =
    73	        ({ base := base, direction := direction } : AxisParallelLine params)
    74	      congr
    75	      funext i
    76	      simp [pointAt, addCoord, zeroCoord]
    77	
    78	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_direction {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    79	    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (t : Fq params) :
    80	    (rebaseAt ℓ t).direction = ℓ.direction :=
    81	  rfl
    82	
    83	/-- The canonical affine parameterization of `throughPoint u i` at parameter
    84	`sampleParameter u i = u i` returns the original point `u`. -/
    85	@[simp] theorem throughPoint_pointAt_sampleParameter {params : Parameters}
    86	    [FieldModel params.q] (u : Point params) (i : Fin params.m) :
    87	    (throughPoint (params := params) u i).pointAt
    88	        (sampleParameter (params := params) u i) = u := by
    89	  ext j
    90	  by_cases h : j = i
    91	  · subst h
    92	    simp [throughPoint, pointAt, sampleParameter, addCoord, zeroCoord]
    93	  · simp [throughPoint, pointAt, h]
    94	
    95	/-- Rebasing the canonical line `throughPoint u i` at its sample parameter yields
    96	the axis-parallel line with base `u` and direction `i`. -/
    97	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_throughPoint_sampleParameter {params : Parameters}
    98	    [FieldModel params.q] (u : Point params) (i : Fin params.m) :
    99	    rebaseAt (throughPoint (params := params) u i)
   100	        (sampleParameter (params := params) u i) =
   101	      { base := u, direction := i } := by
   102	  change
   103	    ({ base :=
   104	        (throughPoint (params := params) u i).pointAt
   105	          (sampleParameter (params := params) u i)
   106	       direction := i } : AxisParallelLine params) =
   107	      { base := u, direction := i }
   108	  congr
   109	  exact throughPoint_pointAt_sampleParameter u i
   110	
   111	/-- Embed an axis-parallel line into the slice at height `x`. -/
   112	def appendAtHeight (params : Parameters)
   113	    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (x : Fq params) : AxisParallelLine params.next where
   114	  base := appendPoint params ℓ.base x
   115	  direction := embedCoord params ℓ.direction
   116	
   117	@[simp] theorem appendAtHeight_rebaseAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   118	    (ℓ : AxisParallelLine params) (t x : Fq params) :
   119	    appendAtHeight params (rebaseAt ℓ t) x =
   120	      rebaseAt (appendAtHeight params ℓ x) t := by
   121	  cases ℓ with
   122	  | mk base direction =>
   123	      change
   124	        ({ base :=
   125	             appendPoint params
   126	               (({ base := base, direction := direction } : AxisParallelLine params).pointAt t) x,
   127	           direction := embedCoord params direction } : AxisParallelLine params.next) =
   128	        ({ base :=
   129	             ({ base := appendPoint params base x,
   130	                direction := embedCoord params direction } :
   131	                AxisParallelLine params.next).pointAt t,
   132	           direction := embedCoord params direction } : AxisParallelLine params.next)
   133	      congr
   134	      funext i
   135	      by_cases hdir : i = embedCoord params direction
   136	      · subst i
   137	        simp [appendPoint, pointAt, embedCoord]
   138	        rfl
   139	      · by_cases hi : i.1 < params.m
   140	        · have hdir' : (⟨i.1, hi⟩ : Fin params.m) ≠ direction := by
   141	            intro h
   142	            apply hdir
   143	            apply Fin.ext
   144	            simpa [embedCoord] using congrArg Fin.val h
   145	          simp [appendPoint, pointAt, hi, hdir, hdir']
   146	        · simp [appendPoint, pointAt, hi, hdir]
   147	
   148	end AxisParallelLine
   149	
   150	end MIPStarRE.LDT

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.QuantumState
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Core submeasurement structures for the low individual degree test
     5	
     6	Foundational measurement, submeasurement, and projective-measurement structures.
     7	-/
     8	
     9	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    10	
    11	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    12	
    13	/-- A paper-local submeasurement with outcomes in `α` and Hilbert space index `ι`.
    14	
    15	There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: the zero family satisfies
    16	these raw axioms, but using it as an ambient default would silently turn later
    17	arguments into vacuous submeasurement statements. -/
    18	structure SubMeas (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
    19	  outcome : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := fun _ => 0
    20	  total : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 0
    21	  outcome_pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ outcome a
    22	  sum_eq_total : ∑ a, outcome a = total
    23	  total_le_one : total ≤ 1
    24	
    25	/-- A paper-local measurement: a POVM whose PSD effects sum to the identity. -/
    26	structure Measurement (α : Type*) (ι : Type*) [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	    extends SubMeas α ι where
    28	  total_eq_one : total = 1
    29	
    30	set_option linter.unusedFintypeInType false in
    31	open scoped Classical in
    32	/-- For a trivial distinguished-outcome measurement, every outcome operator is
    33	positive semidefinite: `0 ≤ if a = a₀ then 1 else 0`. -/
    34	private theorem Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_outcome_pos
    35	    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a₀ a : α) :
    36	    (0 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) ≤ if a = a₀ then 1 else 0 := by
    37	  by_cases h : a = a₀ <;> simp [h]
    38	
    39	open scoped Classical in
    40	/-- ⚠️ DEGENERATE — Construct a trivial measurement where only the distinguished
    41	outcome `a₀` is the identity and all other outcomes are zero.
    42	
    43	This is a valid POVM but highly degenerate: it is only used in vacuous
    44	fallback branches of the proof where the error bound is ≥ 1 (see
    45	`Test/MainTheorem.lean:mainFormal_trivial_witness`).
    46	
    47	Call this function explicitly with a chosen outcome.  There is intentionally no
    48	ambient `Inhabited (Measurement α ι)` instance: choosing a hidden
    49	`default : α` would make degenerate witnesses available to paper-facing
    50	existential statements without displaying the selected outcome. -/
    51	noncomputable def Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome
    52	    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
    53	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    54	    (a₀ : α) : Measurement α ι where
    55	  toSubMeas := {
    56	    outcome := fun a => if a = a₀ then 1 else 0
    57	    total := 1
    58	    outcome_pos := fun a => Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_outcome_pos a₀ a
    59	    sum_eq_total :=
    60	      (Finset.sum_ite_eq' Finset.univ a₀ fun _ => 1).trans (if_pos (Finset.mem_univ a₀))
    61	    total_le_one := le_rfl
    62	  }
    63	  total_eq_one := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- A paper-local projective submeasurement (each effect is idempotent).
    66	
    67	There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: any such default would
    68	again collapse to the degenerate zero family. -/
    69	structure ProjSubMeas (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    70	    extends SubMeas α ι where
    71	  proj : ∀ a, outcome a * outcome a = outcome a
    72	
    73	/-- A paper-local projective measurement (complete POVM + projective). -/
    74	structure ProjMeas (α : Type*) (ι : Type*) [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    75	    extends Measurement α ι where
    76	  proj : ∀ a, outcome a * outcome a = outcome a
    77	
    78	/-- For a trivial distinguished-outcome projective measurement, every outcome operator
    79	is idempotent. -/
    80	private theorem ProjMeas.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_proj
    81	    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (a₀ a : α) :
    82	    (Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome (ι := ι) a₀).outcome a *
    83	        (Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome (ι := ι) a₀).outcome a =
    84	      (Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome (ι := ι) a₀).outcome a := by
    85	  classical
    86	  by_cases h : a = a₀ <;> simp [Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome, h]
    87	
    88	/-- ⚠️ DEGENERATE — Construct a trivial projective measurement where only the
    89	distinguished outcome `a₀` is the identity and all other outcomes are zero.
    90	
    91	This is a valid projective POVM but highly degenerate: see the discussion at
    92	`Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome`.  Prefer calling this function
    93	explicitly (with a chosen outcome) rather than relying on the ambient
    94	`Inhabited` instance.  As for `Measurement`, there is intentionally no ambient
    95	`Inhabited (ProjMeas α ι)` instance. -/
    96	noncomputable def ProjMeas.trivialDistinguishedOutcome
    97	    {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
    98	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    99	    (a₀ : α) : ProjMeas α ι where
   100	  toMeasurement := Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome a₀
   101	  proj := ProjMeas.trivialDistinguishedOutcome_proj a₀
   102	
   103	/-! ### Derived properties -/
   104	
   105	/-- Two submeasurements are equal when they have the same outcome operators and
   106	the same total operator. -/
   107	@[ext] theorem SubMeas.ext {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   108	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   109	    {A B : SubMeas α ι}
   110	    (houtcome : ∀ a : α, A.outcome a = B.outcome a)
   111	    (htotal : A.total = B.total) :
   112	    A = B := by
   113	  cases A with
   114	  | mk outcomeA totalA posA sumA leA =>
   115	      cases B with
   116	      | mk outcomeB totalB posB sumB leB =>
   117	          have houtcome' : outcomeA = outcomeB := by
   118	            funext a
   119	            exact houtcome a
   120	          cases houtcome'
   121	          cases htotal
   122	          cases Subsingleton.elim posB posA
   123	          cases Subsingleton.elim sumB sumA
   124	          cases Subsingleton.elim leB leA
   125	          rfl
   126	
   127	/-- Two measurements are equal when they have the same outcome operators. -/
   128	@[ext] theorem Measurement.ext {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   129	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   130	    {A B : Measurement α ι}
   131	    (houtcome : ∀ a : α, A.outcome a = B.outcome a) :
   132	    A = B := by
   133	  cases A with
   134	  | mk AtoSubMeas AtotalEqOne =>
   135	      cases B with
   136	      | mk BtoSubMeas BtotalEqOne =>
   137	          have hsub : AtoSubMeas = BtoSubMeas := by
   138	            apply SubMeas.ext
   139	            · intro a
   140	              simpa using houtcome a
   141	            · calc
   142	                AtoSubMeas.total = 1 := AtotalEqOne
   143	                _ = BtoSubMeas.total := BtotalEqOne.symm
   144	          cases hsub
   145	          cases Subsingleton.elim BtotalEqOne AtotalEqOne
   146	          rfl
   147	
   148	/-- Two projective measurements are equal when they have the same outcome
   149	operators. -/
   150	@[ext] theorem ProjMeas.ext {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   151	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   152	    {A B : ProjMeas α ι}
   153	    (houtcome : ∀ a : α, A.outcome a = B.outcome a) :
   154	    A = B := by
   155	  cases A with
   156	  | mk AtoMeasurement Aproj =>
   157	      cases B with
   158	      | mk BtoMeasurement Bproj =>
   159	          have hmeas : AtoMeasurement = BtoMeasurement := by
   160	            apply Measurement.ext
   161	            intro a
   162	            simpa using houtcome a
   163	          cases hmeas
   164	          cases Subsingleton.elim Bproj Aproj
   165	          rfl
   166	
   167	/-- A one-outcome submeasurement associated to a single positive operator
   168	bounded by the identity. -/
   169	def SubMeas.singleOutcome {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   170	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) (hA_pos : 0 ≤ A) (hA_le_one : A ≤ 1) :
   171	    SubMeas Unit ι where
   172	  outcome := fun _ => A
   173	  total := A
   174	  outcome_pos := fun _ => hA_pos
   175	  sum_eq_total := Fintype.sum_unique fun _ => A
   176	  total_le_one := hA_le_one
   177	
   178	@[simp] theorem SubMeas.singleOutcome_outcome {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   179	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) (hA_pos : 0 ≤ A) (hA_le_one : A ≤ 1)
   180	    (u : Unit) :
   181	    (SubMeas.singleOutcome (ι := ι) A hA_pos hA_le_one).outcome u = A :=
   182	  rfl
   183	
   184	@[simp] theorem SubMeas.singleOutcome_total {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   185	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) (hA_pos : 0 ≤ A) (hA_le_one : A ≤ 1) :
   186	    (SubMeas.singleOutcome (ι := ι) A hA_pos hA_le_one).total = A :=
   187	  rfl
   188	
   189	/-- PSD outcomes are Hermitian. -/
   190	theorem SubMeas.outcome_hermitian {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   191	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   192	    (A : SubMeas α ι) (a : α) :
   193	    (A.outcome a)ᴴ = A.outcome a :=
   194	  (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp (A.outcome_pos a)).isHermitian.eq
   195	
   196	/-- PSD outcomes are Hermitian. -/
   197	theorem Measurement.outcome_hermitian {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   198	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   199	    (M : Measurement α ι) (a : α) :
   200	    (M.outcome a)ᴴ = M.outcome a :=
   201	  SubMeas.outcome_hermitian M.toSubMeas a
   202	
   203	/-- Each POVM element is bounded by the identity: `outcome a ≤ 1`.
   204	Proof: `outcome a = 1 - ∑_{b ≠ a} outcome b ≤ 1` since all terms are PSD. -/
   205	theorem Measurement.outcome_le_one {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   206	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   207	    (M : Measurement α ι) (a : α) :
   208	    M.outcome a ≤ 1 := by
   209	  calc M.outcome a
   210	      ≤ ∑ i : α, M.outcome i :=
   211	        Finset.single_le_sum (fun i _ => M.outcome_pos i) (Finset.mem_univ a)
   212	    _ = 1 := by
   213	        rw [M.sum_eq_total, M.total_eq_one]
   214	
   215	/-- The outcome operators of a measurement sum to the identity. -/
   216	theorem Measurement.sum_eq {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   217	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   218	    (M : Measurement α ι) :
   219	    ∑ a, M.outcome a = 1 := by
   220	  rw [M.sum_eq_total, M.total_eq_one]
   221	
   222	/-- A submeasurement is complete exactly when its outcome operators sum to `1`. -/
   223	theorem SubMeas.sum_eq_one_iff_total_eq_one {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   224	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   225	    (A : SubMeas α ι) :
   226	    (∑ a, A.outcome a = 1) ↔ A.total = 1 := by
   227	  simp [A.sum_eq_total]
   228	
   229	/-- Promote a complete submeasurement to a measurement.
   230	
   231	This is the explicit bridge from the paper's sub-measurement convention
   232	`∑ a, A_a ≤ I` to the POVM convention `∑ a, A_a = I`: callers must supply the
   233	completion proof rather than relying on a degenerate default. -/
   234	def SubMeas.toMeasurement {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   235	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   236	    (A : SubMeas α ι) (hcomplete : A.total = 1) :
   237	    Measurement α ι where
   238	  toSubMeas := A
   239	  total_eq_one := hcomplete
   240	
   241	@[simp] theorem SubMeas.toMeasurement_toSubMeas {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   242	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   243	    (A : SubMeas α ι) (hcomplete : A.total = 1) :
   244	    (A.toMeasurement hcomplete).toSubMeas = A :=
   245	  rfl
   246	
   247	@[simp] theorem SubMeas.toMeasurement_outcome {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   248	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   249	    (A : SubMeas α ι) (hcomplete : A.total = 1) (a : α) :
   250	    (A.toMeasurement hcomplete).outcome a = A.outcome a :=
   251	  rfl
   252	
   253	/-- Every submeasurement outcome is bounded by the total operator. -/
   254	theorem SubMeas.outcome_le_total {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   255	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   256	    (A : SubMeas α ι) (a : α) :
   257	    A.outcome a ≤ A.total := by
   258	  calc A.outcome a
   259	      ≤ ∑ i : α, A.outcome i :=
   260	        Finset.single_le_sum (fun i _ => A.outcome_pos i) (Finset.mem_univ a)
   261	    _ = A.total := A.sum_eq_total
   262	
   263	/-- Every submeasurement outcome is bounded by the identity. -/
   264	theorem SubMeas.outcome_le_one {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   265	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   266	    (A : SubMeas α ι) (a : α) :
   267	    A.outcome a ≤ 1 :=
   268	  le_trans (A.outcome_le_total a) A.total_le_one
   269	
   270	/-- The total operator of a submeasurement is PSD. -/
   271	theorem SubMeas.total_nonneg {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   272	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   273	    (A : SubMeas α ι) : 0 ≤ A.total := by
   274	  rw [← A.sum_eq_total]
   275	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => A.outcome_pos a
   276	
   277	/-- Projective submeasurement outcomes are Hermitian (PSD from idempotence). -/
   278	theorem ProjSubMeas.outcome_hermitian {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   279	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   280	    (P : ProjSubMeas α ι) (a : α) :
   281	    (P.outcome a)ᴴ = P.outcome a :=
   282	  SubMeas.outcome_hermitian P.toSubMeas a
   283	
   284	/-- Each projective outcome is absorbed by the total operator. -/
   285	theorem ProjSubMeas.outcome_mul_total_eq_outcome {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   286	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   287	    (P : ProjSubMeas α ι) (a : α) :
   288	    P.outcome a * P.total = P.outcome a := by
   289	  let Pa := P.outcome a
   290	  let R : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 1 - P.total
   291	  have hPa_herm : Paᴴ = Pa := by
   292	    simpa [Pa] using P.outcome_hermitian a
   293	  have hPa_star : IsStarProjection Pa :=
   294	    isStarProjection_iff'.2 ⟨by simpa [Pa] using P.proj a, hPa_herm⟩
   295	  have hR_nonneg : 0 ≤ R := by
   296	    simpa [R] using sub_nonneg.mpr P.total_le_one
   297	  have hR_le_self : R ≤ 1 - Pa := by
   298	    simpa [R, Pa] using
   299	      sub_le_sub_left (P.outcome_le_total a) (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι)
   300	  have hPaRPa_nonneg : 0 ≤ Pa * R * Pa := by
   301	    exact IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate_nonneg hR_nonneg hPa_herm
   302	  have hPa_one_sub_Pa : Pa * (1 - Pa) * Pa = 0 := by
   303	    rw [hPa_star.mul_one_sub_self, zero_mul]
   304	  have hPaRPa_eq_zero : Pa * R * Pa = 0 := by
   305	    apply le_antisymm
   306	    · calc
   307	        Pa * R * Pa ≤ Pa * (1 - Pa) * Pa := by
   308	          exact IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate_le_conjugate hR_le_self hPa_herm
   309	        _ = 0 := hPa_one_sub_Pa
   310	    · simpa using hPaRPa_nonneg
   311	  have hP_total_herm : P.totalᴴ = P.total := by
   312	    exact (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp P.total_nonneg).isHermitian.eq
   313	  have hR_herm : Rᴴ = R := by
   314	    simp [R, hP_total_herm]
   315	  have hR_sq_le : R * R ≤ R := by
   316	    have hR_le_one : R ≤ 1 := by
   317	      simpa [R] using sub_le_self (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) P.total_nonneg
   318	    exact MIPStarRE.Quantum.sq_le_self hR_nonneg hR_le_one
   319	  have hRPa_conj_mul : (R * Pa)ᴴ * (R * Pa) = Pa * (R * R) * Pa := by
   320	    calc
   321	      (R * Pa)ᴴ * (R * Pa) = (Paᴴ * Rᴴ) * (R * Pa) := by
   322	        simp [Matrix.conjTranspose_mul]
   323	      _ = Pa * (R * R) * Pa := by simp [hPa_herm, hR_herm, mul_assoc]
   324	  have hRPa_eq_zero : R * Pa = 0 := by
   325	    apply Matrix.conjTranspose_mul_self_eq_zero.mp
   326	    rw [hRPa_conj_mul]
   327	    apply le_antisymm
   328	    · calc
   329	        Pa * (R * R) * Pa ≤ Pa * R * Pa := by
   330	          exact IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate_le_conjugate hR_sq_le hPa_herm
   331	        _ = 0 := hPaRPa_eq_zero
   332	    · have hnonneg : 0 ≤ Pa * (R * R) * Pa := by
   333	        exact IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate_nonneg
   334	          (show 0 ≤ R * R by
   335	            exact Commute.mul_nonneg hR_nonneg hR_nonneg (Commute.refl R))
   336	          hPa_herm
   337	      simpa using hnonneg
   338	  calc
   339	    P.outcome a * P.total = Pa * (1 - R) := by
   340	      simp [Pa, R, sub_eq_add_neg, add_comm, add_left_comm]
   341	    _ = Pa - Pa * R := by rw [mul_sub, mul_one]
   342	    _ = Pa := by
   343	          have : Pa * R = 0 := by
   344	            simpa [hPa_herm, hR_herm] using congrArg Matrix.conjTranspose hRPa_eq_zero
   345	          simp [this]
   346	    _ = P.outcome a := by rfl
   347	
   348	/-- The total operator of a projective submeasurement is itself a projector. -/
   349	theorem ProjSubMeas.total_proj {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   350	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   351	    (P : ProjSubMeas α ι) :
   352	    P.total * P.total = P.total := by
   353	  calc
   354	    P.total * P.total = (∑ a : α, P.outcome a) * P.total := by rw [P.sum_eq_total]
   355	    _ = ∑ a : α, P.outcome a * P.total := by rw [Matrix.sum_mul]
   356	    _ = ∑ a : α, P.outcome a := by
   357	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   358	          intro a _ha
   359	          exact P.outcome_mul_total_eq_outcome a
   360	    _ = P.total := P.sum_eq_total
   361	
   362	/-- Distinct outcomes of a projective submeasurement are orthogonal. -/
   363	theorem ProjSubMeas.outcome_orthogonal {α : Type*}
   364	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι]
   365	    [DecidableEq ι]
   366	    (P : ProjSubMeas α ι) (a b : α) (hab : a ≠ b) :
   367	    P.outcome a * P.outcome b = 0 := by
   368	  classical
   369	  set Pa := P.outcome a
   370	  set Pb := P.outcome b
   371	  have hsum : Pa + Pb ≤ P.total := by
   372	    calc
   373	      Pa + Pb
   374	        = ∑ i ∈ ({a, b} : Finset α), P.outcome i := by
   375	            simp [Pa, Pb, hab]
   376	      _ ≤ ∑ i : α, P.outcome i := by
   377	            exact Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg
   378	              (by simp)
   379	              (fun i _ _ => P.outcome_pos i)
   380	      _ = P.total := P.sum_eq_total
   381	  have hPb_le : Pb ≤ 1 - Pa := by
   382	    calc
   383	      Pb = Pa + Pb - Pa := by abel
   384	      _ ≤ P.total - Pa := by
   385	          exact sub_le_sub_right hsum Pa
   386	      _ ≤ 1 - Pa := by
   387	          exact sub_le_sub_right P.total_le_one Pa
   388	  have hPa_herm : Paᴴ = Pa := P.outcome_hermitian a
   389	  have hPb_herm : Pbᴴ = Pb := P.outcome_hermitian b
   390	  have hPa_star : IsStarProjection Pa :=
   391	    isStarProjection_iff'.2 ⟨by simpa [Pa] using P.proj a, hPa_herm⟩
   392	  have hPaPbPa_nonneg : 0 ≤ Pa * Pb * Pa :=
   393	    IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate_nonneg (P.outcome_pos b) hPa_herm
   394	  have hPa_idem : Pa * (1 - Pa) * Pa = 0 := by
   395	    rw [hPa_star.mul_one_sub_self, zero_mul]
   396	  have hPaPbPa_eq_zero : Pa * Pb * Pa = 0 := by
   397	    apply le_antisymm
   398	    · calc
   399	        Pa * Pb * Pa ≤ Pa * (1 - Pa) * Pa :=
   400	          IsSelfAdjoint.conjugate_le_conjugate hPb_le hPa_herm

1	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Order
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Block-diagonal finite matrix operators
     5	
     6	This module contains block-diagonal trace and positive-semidefinite order facts
     7	for finite complex matrices.  The canonical SDP block algebra in Section 9 uses
     8	these lemmas to compare the paper's block form with Mathlib's
     9	`Matrix.blockDiagonal`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder Matrix.Norms.Elementwise
    13	open WithLp
    14	
    15	namespace Matrix
    16	
    17	/-- A block-diagonal matrix is the sum of its blocks tensored with the
    18	coordinate projections on the block index. -/
    19	theorem blockDiagonal_eq_sum_kronecker_diagonal {o m : Type*}
    20	    [Fintype o] [DecidableEq o] [Finite m] (B : o → Matrix m m ℂ) :
    21	    Matrix.blockDiagonal B =
    22	      ∑ b : o, Matrix.kronecker (B b)
    23	        (Matrix.diagonal fun c : o => if c = b then (1 : ℂ) else 0) := by
    24	  classical
    25	  letI : Fintype m := Fintype.ofFinite m
    26	  ext x y
    27	  rcases x with ⟨i, bx⟩
    28	  rcases y with ⟨j, cy⟩
    29	  rw [Matrix.sum_apply]
    30	  by_cases hxy : bx = cy
    31	  · subst cy
    32	    simp [Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply]
    33	  · simp [Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply, Matrix.kronecker, Matrix.kroneckerMap_apply, hxy]
    34	
    35	/-- `Matrix.blockDiagonal` as a linear map.
    36	
    37	Mathlib provides `Matrix.blockDiagonalAddMonoidHom` and
    38	`Matrix.blockDiagonal_smul`; this declaration packages these two facts in the
    39	linear form needed by finite-dimensional block SDP arguments. -/
    40	def blockDiagonalLinearMap (R : Type*) (m n o α : Type*)
    41	    [Semiring R] [DecidableEq o] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α] :
    42	    (o → Matrix m n α) →ₗ[R] Matrix (m × o) (n × o) α where
    43	  toFun := Matrix.blockDiagonal
    44	  map_add' := Matrix.blockDiagonal_add
    45	  map_smul' := Matrix.blockDiagonal_smul
    46	
    47	@[simp]
    48	theorem blockDiagonalLinearMap_apply (R : Type*) (m n o α : Type*)
    49	    [Semiring R] [DecidableEq o] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α]
    50	    (B : o → Matrix m n α) :
    51	    Matrix.blockDiagonalLinearMap R m n o α B = Matrix.blockDiagonal B :=
    52	  rfl
    53	
    54	/-- A block-diagonal complex matrix is positive semidefinite when all of its
    55	diagonal blocks are positive semidefinite. -/
    56	theorem blockDiagonal_nonneg {o m : Type*}
    57	    [Finite o] [DecidableEq o] [Finite m]
    58	    (B : o → Matrix m m ℂ) (hB : ∀ b, 0 ≤ B b) :
    59	    0 ≤ Matrix.blockDiagonal B := by
    60	  classical
    61	  letI : Fintype o := Fintype.ofFinite o
    62	  letI : Fintype m := Fintype.ofFinite m
    63	  rw [Matrix.blockDiagonal_eq_sum_kronecker_diagonal B]
    64	  exact Finset.sum_nonneg fun b _ =>
    65	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.kronecker_nonneg (hB b) (by
    66	      refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    67	      exact Matrix.PosSemidef.diagonal <| by
    68	        intro c
    69	        by_cases hc : c = b <;> simp [hc])
    70	
    71	/-- A block-diagonal complex matrix is positive semidefinite exactly when each
    72	of its diagonal blocks is positive semidefinite. -/
    73	theorem blockDiagonal_nonneg_iff {o m : Type*}
    74	    [Finite o] [DecidableEq o] [Finite m]
    75	    (B : o → Matrix m m ℂ) :
    76	    0 ≤ Matrix.blockDiagonal B ↔ ∀ b, 0 ≤ B b := by
    77	  classical
    78	  letI : Fintype o := Fintype.ofFinite o
    79	  letI : Fintype m := Fintype.ofFinite m
    80	  constructor
    81	  · intro hB b
    82	    refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    83	    let e : m → m × o := fun i => (i, b)
    84	    have hsub :
    85	        ((Matrix.blockDiagonal B).submatrix e e).PosSemidef :=
    86	      (Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mp hB).submatrix e
    87	    have hEq : (Matrix.blockDiagonal B).submatrix e e = B b := by
    88	      ext i j
    89	      simp [e, Matrix.blockDiagonal_apply_eq]
    90	    simpa [hEq] using hsub
    91	  · exact Matrix.blockDiagonal_nonneg B
    92	
    93	end Matrix

1	import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.AxisParallelLine
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Diagonal lines for the low individual degree test
     5	
     6	Diagonal-line geometry and rebasing operations.
     7	
     8	## References
     9	
    10	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex`
    11	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch02_test.tex`
    12	-/
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    15	
    16	/-- A genuinely affine diagonal line in `F_q^m`. -/
    17	structure DiagonalLine (params : Parameters) where
    18	  base : Point params
    19	  direction : Point params
    20	
    21	deriving instance DecidableEq, Inhabited for DiagonalLine
    22	
    23	namespace DiagonalLine
    24	
    25	/-- The canonical affine parameterization `t ↦ base + t · direction`. -/
    26	def pointAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    27	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) : Fq params → Point params :=
    28	  fun t => addPoint ℓ.base (smulPoint t ℓ.direction)
    29	
    30	/-- The support of the nonzero coordinates of a direction vector. -/
    31	noncomputable def nonzeroDirectionSupport {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    32	    (v : Point params) : Finset (Fin params.m) :=
    33	  Finset.univ.filter fun i => v i ≠ zeroCoord
    34	
    35	/-- The least nonzero coordinate of a direction vector, when one exists. -/
    36	noncomputable def firstNonzeroCoord? {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    37	    (v : Point params) : Option (Fin params.m) :=
    38	  open Classical in
    39	  let s := nonzeroDirectionSupport (params := params) v
    40	  if hs : s.Nonempty then some (s.min' hs) else none
    41	
    42	/-- Normalize a direction vector so its first nonzero coordinate becomes `1`. -/
    43	noncomputable def normalizeDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    44	    (v : Point params) : Point params :=
    45	  open Classical in
    46	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    47	    | none => zeroPoint
    48	    | some i => smulPoint (invCoord (v i)) v
    49	
    50	/-- Canonical geometric diagonal line through `u` in direction `v`.
    51	
    52	For nonzero `v`, we normalize by the first nonzero coordinate and shift the
    53	base point so that this pivot coordinate is `0`. The degenerate `v = 0` case is
    54	kept as the singleton line through `u`. -/
    55	noncomputable def throughPointDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    56	    (u v : Point params) : DiagonalLine params :=
    57	  open Classical in
    58	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    59	    | none => { base := u, direction := zeroPoint }
    60	    | some i =>
    61	        let w := normalizeDirection (params := params) v
    62	        let t := u i
    63	        { base := fun j => subCoord (u j) (mulCoord t (w j))
    64	          direction := w }
    65	
    66	/-- Affine parameter of the sampled point on the canonical diagonal line through
    67	`u` in direction `v`. -/
    68	noncomputable def sampleParameter {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    69	    (u v : Point params) : Fq params :=
    70	  open Classical in
    71	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    72	    | none => zeroCoord
    73	    | some i => u i
    74	
    75	@[simp] theorem throughPoint_pointAt_sampleParameter {params : Parameters}
    76	    [FieldModel params.q] (u : Point params) (i : Fin params.m) :
    77	    (AxisParallelLine.throughPoint (params := params) u i).pointAt
    78	        (AxisParallelLine.sampleParameter (params := params) u i) = u := by
    79	  funext j
    80	  by_cases h : j = i
    81	  · subst h
    82	    unfold AxisParallelLine.pointAt AxisParallelLine.throughPoint
    83	    simp [AxisParallelLine.sampleParameter, addCoord, zeroCoord]
    84	  · simp [AxisParallelLine.throughPoint, AxisParallelLine.pointAt, h]
    85	
    86	@[simp] theorem throughPointDirection_pointAt_sampleParameter {params : Parameters}
    87	    [FieldModel params.q] (u v : Point params) :
    88	    (DiagonalLine.throughPointDirection (params := params) u v).pointAt
    89	        (DiagonalLine.sampleParameter (params := params) u v) = u := by
    90	  classical
    91	  unfold DiagonalLine.throughPointDirection DiagonalLine.sampleParameter
    92	  split
    93	  · funext j
    94	    simp [DiagonalLine.pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, zeroPoint,
    95	      zeroCoord, addCoord, mulCoord]
    96	  · rename_i i
    97	    funext j
    98	    simp [DiagonalLine.pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, subCoord, addCoord, mulCoord]
    99	
   100	/-- Rebase a diagonal line so that the old point `ℓ.pointAt t` becomes the new base point. -/
   101	def rebaseAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   102	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t : Fq params) : DiagonalLine params where
   103	  base := ℓ.pointAt t
   104	  direction := ℓ.direction
   105	
   106	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_pointAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   107	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t : Fq params) :
   108	    (rebaseAt ℓ t).pointAt zeroCoord = ℓ.pointAt t := by
   109	  ext i
   110	  simp [rebaseAt, pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, addCoord, mulCoord, zeroCoord]
   111	
   112	theorem rebaseAt_pointAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   113	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) (t s : Fq params) :
   114	    (rebaseAt ℓ t).pointAt s = ℓ.pointAt (addCoord t s) := by
   115	  ext i
   116	  simp only [pointAt, addPoint, addCoord, rebaseAt, smulPoint, mulCoord, decode_encodeScalar]
   117	  rw [← encode_decodeScalar (ℓ.base i)]
   118	  congr 1
   119	  ring_nf
   120	
   121	@[simp] theorem rebaseAt_zero {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
   122	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) :
   123	    rebaseAt ℓ zeroCoord = ℓ := by
   124	  cases ℓ with
   125	  | mk base direction =>
   126	      change
   127	        ({ base :=
   128	             ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params).pointAt zeroCoord,
   129	           direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params) =
   130	        ({ base := base, direction := direction } : DiagonalLine params)
   131	      congr
   132	      funext i
   133	      simp [pointAt, addPoint, smulPoint, addCoord, mulCoord, zeroCoord]

   135	theorem rebaseAt_rebase {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement

    96	namespace Measurement

   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement

   251	                · simp [hfa]
   252	              · simp
   253	            · have hzero :
   254	                  (∑ b : β,
   255	                    if g b = c ∧ f a = b then
   256	                      A.outcome a
   257	                    else (0 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι)) = 0 := by
   258	                refine Finset.sum_eq_zero ?_
   259	                intro b _
   260	                by_cases hfa : f a = b
   261	                · subst b
   262	                  simp [hgc]
   263	                · simp [hfa]
   264	              simp [hgc, hzero]
   265	    _ = (postprocess A (fun a => g (f a))).outcome c := by
   266	          simp [postprocess, Finset.sum_filter]
   267	
   268	end SubMeas
   269	
   270	namespace Measurement
   271	
   272	/-- Transport a measurement along an equivalence of outcome types. -/
   273	noncomputable def transport {α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   274	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   275	    (e : α ≃ β) (A : Measurement α ι) :
   276	    Measurement β ι where
   277	  toSubMeas := SubMeas.transport e A.toSubMeas
   278	  total_eq_one := A.total_eq_one
   279	
   280	end Measurement
   281	
   282	namespace ProjSubMeas
   283	
   284	/-- Transport a projective submeasurement along an equivalence of outcome types. -/
   285	noncomputable def transport {α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   286	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   287	    (e : α ≃ β) (A : ProjSubMeas α ι) :
   288	    ProjSubMeas β ι where
   289	  toSubMeas := SubMeas.transport e A.toSubMeas
   290	  proj := fun b => A.proj (e.symm b)
   291	
   292	/-- Postprocessing a projective submeasurement preserves outcome projectivity. -/
   293	theorem postprocess_outcome_proj {α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   294	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   295	    (P : ProjSubMeas α ι) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   296	    (postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b * (postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b =
   297	      (postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b := by
   298	  classical
   299	  let fiber : Finset α := Finset.univ.filter fun a => f a = b
   300	  calc
   301	    (postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b * (postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b
   302	      = (∑ a ∈ fiber, P.outcome a) * (∑ a' ∈ fiber, P.outcome a') := by
   303	          simp [postprocess, fiber]
   304	    _ = ∑ a ∈ fiber, ∑ a' ∈ fiber, P.outcome a * P.outcome a' := by
   305	          rw [Finset.sum_mul]
   306	          simp_rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   307	    _ = ∑ a ∈ fiber, ∑ a' ∈ fiber, if a' = a then P.outcome a else 0 := by
   308	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   309	          intro a ha
   310	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   311	          intro a' ha'
   312	          by_cases h : a' = a
   313	          · subst h
   314	            simp [P.proj]
   315	          · have hne : a ≠ a' := fun h' => h h'.symm
   316	            simp [ProjSubMeas.outcome_orthogonal P _ _ hne, h]
   317	    _ = ∑ a ∈ fiber, P.outcome a := by
   318	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   319	          intro a ha
   320	          simp [fiber, ha]
   321	    _ = (postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b := by
   322	          simp [postprocess, fiber]
   323	
   324	end ProjSubMeas
   325	
   326	namespace ProjMeas
   327	
   328	/-- Transport a projective measurement along an equivalence of outcome types. -/
   329	noncomputable def transport {α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   330	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   331	    (e : α ≃ β) (A : ProjMeas α ι) :
   332	    ProjMeas β ι where
   333	  toMeasurement := Measurement.transport e A.toMeasurement
   334	  proj := fun b => A.proj (e.symm b)
   335	
   336	@[simp] theorem transport_trivialDistinguishedOutcome {α ι : Type*}
   337	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   338	    (e : α ≃ α) (a₀ : α) :
   339	    transport e (trivialDistinguishedOutcome (ι := ι) a₀) =
   340	      trivialDistinguishedOutcome (e a₀) := by
   341	  classical
   342	  ext a i j
   343	  by_cases h : a = e a₀
   344	  · simp [transport, Measurement.transport, SubMeas.transport,
   345	      trivialDistinguishedOutcome, Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome, h]
   346	  · have hs : e.symm a ≠ a₀ := by
   347	      intro hs
   348	      apply h
   349	      calc
   350	        a = e (e.symm a) := by simp
   351	        _ = e a₀ := by rw [hs]
   352	    simp [transport, Measurement.transport, SubMeas.transport,
   353	      trivialDistinguishedOutcome, Measurement.trivialDistinguishedOutcome, h, hs]
   354	
   355	@[simp] theorem transport_toSubMeas {α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   356	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   357	    (e : α ≃ β) (A : ProjMeas α ι) :
   358	    (transport e A).toSubMeas = SubMeas.transport e A.toSubMeas :=
   359	  rfl
   360	
   361	/-- Postprocess a projective measurement along a relabeling of the outcome type.
   362	
   363	The fiber of each output value is a sum of mutually orthogonal projectors, so
   364	postprocessing preserves projectivity as well as completeness. -/
   365	noncomputable def postprocess {α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   366	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   367	    (A : ProjMeas α ι) (f : α → β) :
   368	    ProjMeas β ι where
   369	  toMeasurement := {
   370	    toSubMeas := MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess A.toSubMeas f
   371	    total_eq_one := A.total_eq_one
   372	  }
   373	  proj := fun b => ProjSubMeas.postprocess_outcome_proj ⟨A.toSubMeas, A.proj⟩ f b
   374	
   375	@[simp] theorem postprocess_toSubMeas {α β : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   376	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   377	    (A : ProjMeas α ι) (f : α → β) :
   378	    (postprocess A f).toSubMeas = MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess A.toSubMeas f :=
   379	  rfl
   380	
   381	end ProjMeas
   382	
   383	/-- Postprocessed outcomes from the same ProjMeas commute. -/
   384	theorem ProjMeas.postprocess_outcome_commute
   385	    {α β γ : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   386	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [Fintype γ]
   387	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   388	    (P : ProjMeas α ι) (f : α → β) (g : α → γ)
   389	    (b : β) (c : γ) :
   390	    (MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b *
   391	      (MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess P.toSubMeas g).outcome c =
   392	    (MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess P.toSubMeas g).outcome c *
   393	      (MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess P.toSubMeas f).outcome b := by
   394	  classical
   395	  simp only [MIPStarRE.LDT.postprocess]
   396	  simp_rw [Finset.sum_mul, Finset.mul_sum]
   397	  rw [Finset.sum_comm]
   398	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun x _ => ?_
   399	  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun y _ => ?_
   400	  exact P.outcome_commute y x
   401	
   402	/-- Complete a submeasurement by adjoining a distinguished failure outcome. -/
   403	noncomputable def completeSubMeas {α : Type*} {ι : Type*}
   404	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   405	    (A : SubMeas α ι) : Measurement (Option α) ι where
   406	  toSubMeas := {
   407	    outcome := fun
   408	      | some a => A.outcome a
   409	      | none => 1 - A.total
   410	    total := 1
   411	    outcome_pos := fun
   412	      | some a => A.outcome_pos a
   413	      | none => sub_nonneg.mpr A.total_le_one
   414	    sum_eq_total := (Fintype.sum_option _).trans <|
   415	      (congrArg (1 - A.total + ·) A.sum_eq_total).trans (sub_add_cancel 1 A.total)
   416	    total_le_one := le_rfl
   417	  }
   418	  total_eq_one := rfl
   419	
   420	/-- Constant indexed family taking the same submeasurement on every question. -/
   421	def constSubMeasFamily {α : Type*} {ι : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   422	    (A : SubMeas α ι) :
   423	    IdxSubMeas Unit α ι :=
   424	  fun _ => A
   425	
   426	/-- Average an indexed submeasurement family against a finite distribution.
   427	
   428	The hypothesis `∑ q ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight q ≤ 1` says that `𝒟` is a sub-probability
   429	distribution (total mass at most `1`); this is all that is needed to keep the
   430	averaged total operator below `1`. -/

560	/-- The trace selected by a fixed model; this is the map denoted `tr` in the
   561	paper's `def:binary-representation`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:298-315`,
   562	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:653-680`. -/
   563	noncomputable def fixedBinTrace {q : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q) : F.K → ZMod 2 :=
   564	  binTrace F.K
   565	
   566	/--
   567	The matrix-trace presentation of `fixedBinTrace`, a statement-level bridge to
   568	Equation `eq:def-trace`.  It is the trace assertion in `def:subfield-trace`,
   569	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:217-232`, paper origin
   570	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:481-502`.  Mathlib's
   571	`Algebra.trace_eq_matrix_trace` supplies the basis-independent equality.
   572	-/
   573	theorem fixedBinTrace_eq_matrixTrace {q ι : ℕ} (F : FixedFieldModel q)
   574	    (b : Module.Basis (Fin ι) (ZMod 2) F.K) (a : F.K) :
   575	    fixedBinTrace F a = (multiplicationTable b a).trace := by

     4	/-!
     5	# The quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file states the external quantum-linearity result used to combine the
     8	binary observables produced in the point analysis.  The statement uses a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, and its conclusion adjoins a finite ancillary
    10	space on which the exactly linear observables act.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`.  The quotation in the
    16	QPBT paper is at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    18	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    31	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    32	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`, quoted at paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    34	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    35	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    36	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    37	
    38	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector. -/
    39	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    40	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    41	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    42	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    43	
    44	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    45	quantity `d_rho(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`. -/
    47	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    48	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    49	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    50	
    51	/-- The quantum linearity theorem imported from Natarajan--Vidick.
    52	
    53	The statement is `thm:linearity` in
    54	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-145`; the QPBT paper quotes
    55	it at
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
    57	
    58	As recorded in `rem:linearity-import` (blueprint lines 147--180), this
    59	provider-faithful form imposes no upper bound on `δ`, preserves the error,
    60	asserts exact linearity for every pair, and averages closeness only over `u`.
    61	The paper quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases closeness pointwise under a
    62	pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three deviations are not
    63	reproduced.  The identity at zero follows later from exact linearity and the
    64	binary-observable condition. -/
    65	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    66	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    67	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    68	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    69	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    70	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    71	    (hcorrelation :
    72	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
    73	        (uniformDistribution
    74	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    75	        (fun pair =>
    76	          (Matrix.trace
    77	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
    78	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
    79	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
    80	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
    81	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
    82	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧
    83	          (∀ u u', L u * L u' = L (u + u')) ∧
    84	          avgOver (uniformDistribution (Fin t → ZMod 2))
    85	              (fun u => stateDepDistSq (L u)
    86	                (heteroKron (O u) (1 : Op ι'))
    87	                (heteroKron ρ (ancProj anc))) ≤ δ := by
    88	  sorry
    89	
    90	end
    91	
    92	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/

   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>

   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite

   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum
