    19	/-! ### Complete block-measurement constructors -/
    20	
    21	/-- Direct-sum measurement obtained by placing Alice's and Bob's complete
    22	measurements on the `Sum.inl` and `Sum.inr` sectors respectively. -/
    23	noncomputable def localDirectSumMeasurement {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    24	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    25	    (MA : Measurement Outcome ιA) (MB : Measurement Outcome ιB) :
    26	    Measurement Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) :=
    27	  ({ outcome := fun a => localDirectSumBlock (MA.outcome a) (MB.outcome a)
    28	     total := localDirectSumBlock MA.total MB.total
    29	     outcome_pos := fun a => localDirectSumBlock_nonneg (MA.outcome_pos a) (MB.outcome_pos a)
    30	     sum_eq_total :=
    31	       (localDirectSumBlock_finset_sum Finset.univ MA.outcome MB.outcome).trans
    32	         (congrArg₂ localDirectSumBlock MA.sum_eq_total MB.sum_eq_total)
    33	     total_le_one :=
    34	       ((congrArg₂ localDirectSumBlock MA.total_eq_one MB.total_eq_one).trans
    35	         localDirectSumBlock_one).le } :
    36	    SubMeas Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)).toMeasurement
    37	    ((congrArg₂ localDirectSumBlock MA.total_eq_one MB.total_eq_one).trans
    38	      localDirectSumBlock_one)
    39	
    40	@[simp] theorem localDirectSumMeasurement_outcome {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    41	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    42	    (MA : Measurement Outcome ιA) (MB : Measurement Outcome ιB) (a : Outcome) :
    43	    (localDirectSumMeasurement MA MB).outcome a =
    44	      localDirectSumBlock (MA.outcome a) (MB.outcome a) :=
    45	  rfl
    46	
    47	@[simp] theorem localDirectSumMeasurement_total {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    48	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    49	    (MA : Measurement Outcome ιA) (MB : Measurement Outcome ιB) :
    50	    (localDirectSumMeasurement MA MB).total = 1 := by
    51	  simp [localDirectSumMeasurement, MA.total_eq_one, MB.total_eq_one]
    52	
    53	/-- Direct-sum projective measurement obtained by block-diagonalizing two
    54	projective measurements with the same outcome type. -/
    55	noncomputable def localDirectSumProjMeas {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    56	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    57	    (MA : ProjMeas Outcome ιA) (MB : ProjMeas Outcome ιB) :
    58	    ProjMeas Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) where
    59	  toMeasurement := localDirectSumMeasurement MA.toMeasurement MB.toMeasurement
    60	  proj := fun a =>
    61	    (localDirectSumBlock_mul _ _ _ _).trans
    62	      (congrArg₂ localDirectSumBlock (MA.proj a) (MB.proj a))
    63	
    64	@[simp] theorem localDirectSumProjMeas_outcome {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    65	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    66	    (MA : ProjMeas Outcome ιA) (MB : ProjMeas Outcome ιB) (a : Outcome) :
    67	    (localDirectSumProjMeas MA MB).outcome a =
    68	      localDirectSumBlock (MA.outcome a) (MB.outcome a) :=
    69	  rfl
    70	
    71	/-- Role-register measurement obtained by placing two complete direct-sum
    72	measurements in the `Role.A` and `Role.B` sectors. -/
    73	noncomputable def roleBlockMeasurement {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    74	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    75	    (MA MB : Measurement Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) :
    76	    Measurement Outcome (RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB) :=
    77	  ({ outcome := fun a => roleBlock (MA.outcome a) (MB.outcome a)
    78	     total := roleBlock MA.total MB.total
    79	     outcome_pos := fun a => roleBlock_nonneg (MA.outcome_pos a) (MB.outcome_pos a)
    80	     sum_eq_total :=
    81	       (roleBlock_finset_sum Finset.univ MA.outcome MB.outcome).trans
    82	         (congrArg₂ roleBlock MA.sum_eq_total MB.sum_eq_total)
    83	     total_le_one :=
    84	       ((congrArg₂ roleBlock MA.total_eq_one MB.total_eq_one).trans roleBlock_one).le } :
    85	    SubMeas Outcome (RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB)).toMeasurement
    86	    ((congrArg₂ roleBlock MA.total_eq_one MB.total_eq_one).trans roleBlock_one)
    87	
    88	@[simp] theorem roleBlockMeasurement_outcome {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    89	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    90	    (MA MB : Measurement Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) (a : Outcome) :
    91	    (roleBlockMeasurement MA MB).outcome a = roleBlock (MA.outcome a) (MB.outcome a) :=
    92	  rfl
    93	
    94	@[simp] theorem roleBlockMeasurement_total {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
    95	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    96	    (MA MB : Measurement Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) :
    97	    (roleBlockMeasurement MA MB).total = 1 := by
    98	  simp [roleBlockMeasurement, MA.total_eq_one, MB.total_eq_one]
    99	
   100	/-- Role-register projective measurement obtained by block-diagonalizing two
   101	complete direct-sum projective measurements. -/
   102	noncomputable def roleBlockProjMeas {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
   103	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   104	    (MA MB : ProjMeas Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) :
   105	    ProjMeas Outcome (RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB) where
   106	  toMeasurement := roleBlockMeasurement MA.toMeasurement MB.toMeasurement
   107	  proj := fun a =>
   108	    (roleBlock_mul _ _ _ _).trans (congrArg₂ roleBlock (MA.proj a) (MB.proj a))
   109	
   110	@[simp] theorem roleBlockProjMeas_outcome {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
   111	    [Fintype Outcome] [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   112	    (MA MB : ProjMeas Outcome (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) (a : Outcome) :
   113	    (roleBlockProjMeas MA MB).outcome a = roleBlock (MA.outcome a) (MB.outcome a) :=
   114	  rfl
   115	
   116	/--
   117	Heterogeneous role-register projective measurement for a two-space strategy.
   118	
   119	The `Role.A` sector acts on Alice's original summand and the `Role.B` sector
   120	acts on Bob's original summand, as in the role-register symmetrization in
   121	`references/ldt-paper/inductive_step.tex:40-59`.  The complementary direct-sum
   122	sectors are filled by the canonical distinguished-outcome projective
   123	measurement.  Those sectors are auxiliary: in the eventual heterogeneous
   124	symmetrized state, the occupied sectors are `(Role.A, Sum.inl _)` on the left
   125	and `(Role.B, Sum.inr _)` on the right, together with their swapped copy. -/
   126	noncomputable def roleRegisterProjMeas {Outcome ιA ιB : Type*}
   127	    [Inhabited Outcome] [Fintype Outcome]
   128	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
   129	    (MA : ProjMeas Outcome ιA) (MB : ProjMeas Outcome ιB) :
   130	    ProjMeas Outcome (RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB) :=
   560	  simp [localDirectSumBlock, Matrix.fromBlocks_add]
   561	
   562	@[simp] theorem localDirectSumBlock_conjTranspose {ιA ιB : Type*}
   563	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιB) :
   564	    (localDirectSumBlock A B)ᴴ = localDirectSumBlock Aᴴ Bᴴ := by
   565	  simp [localDirectSumBlock, Matrix.fromBlocks_conjTranspose]
   566	
   567	@[simp] theorem localDirectSumBlock_mul {ιA ιB : Type*} [Fintype ιA] [Fintype ιB]
   568	    (A₁ A₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) (B₁ B₂ : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιB) :
   569	    localDirectSumBlock A₁ B₁ * localDirectSumBlock A₂ B₂ =
   570	      localDirectSumBlock (A₁ * A₂) (B₁ * B₂) := by
   571	  simp [localDirectSumBlock, Matrix.fromBlocks_multiply]
   572	
   573	/-- A direct sum of positive semidefinite operators is positive semidefinite. -/
   574	theorem localDirectSumBlock_nonneg {ιA ιB : Type*} [Finite ιA] [Finite ιB]
   575	    {A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA} {B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιB}
   576	    (hA : 0 ≤ A) (hB : 0 ≤ B) : 0 ≤ localDirectSumBlock A B := by
   577	  classical
   578	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ιA
   579	  letI := Fintype.ofFinite ιB
   580	  rw [CStarAlgebra.nonneg_iff_eq_star_mul_self] at hA hB ⊢
   581	  rcases hA with ⟨C, hC⟩
   582	  rcases hB with ⟨D, hD⟩
   583	  refine ⟨localDirectSumBlock C D, ?_⟩
   584	  have hC' : A = Cᴴ * C := hC
   585	  have hD' : B = Dᴴ * D := hD
   586	  change localDirectSumBlock A B = (localDirectSumBlock C D)ᴴ * localDirectSumBlock C D
   587	  rw [localDirectSumBlock_conjTranspose, localDirectSumBlock_mul, ← hC', ← hD']
   588	
   589	/-- Finite sums commute through direct-sum blocks.
   590	
   591	This is the completeness calculation for block-diagonal measurements: if
   592	Alice's and Bob's effects each sum to their local totals, then the direct-sum
   593	effects sum to the direct sum of those totals. -/
   594	theorem localDirectSumBlock_finset_sum {α ιA ιB : Type*} (s : Finset α)
   595	    (A : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιA) (B : α → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ιB) :
   596	    ∑ a ∈ s, localDirectSumBlock (A a) (B a) =
   597	      localDirectSumBlock (∑ a ∈ s, A a) (∑ a ∈ s, B a) := by
   598	  classical
   599	  induction s using Finset.induction_on with
   600	  | empty => simp
   601	  | insert a s ha ih =>
   602	      rw [Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha, Finset.sum_insert ha, ih]
   603	      rw [localDirectSumBlock_add]
   604	
   605	private def roleBlockFamily {ιA ιB : Type*}
   606	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) :
   607	    Role → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)
   608	  | Role.A => A
   609	  | Role.B => B
   610	
   611	/-- The role-register block diagonal as a ring homomorphism. -/
   612	private noncomputable def roleBlockRingHom {ιA ιB : Type*}
   613	    [Fintype ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιA] [DecidableEq ιB] :
   614	    (Role → MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) →+*
   615	      MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB) := by
   616	  classical
   617	  exact
   618	    (Matrix.reindexAlgEquiv ℂ ℂ
   619	      (Equiv.prodComm (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) Role)).toRingHom.comp
   620	        (Matrix.blockDiagonalRingHom (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) Role ℂ)
   621	
   622	/-- Role-blocked operator on `Role × (ιA ⊕ ιB)`.
   623	
   624	The first block is used when the role register is `Role.A`; the second block is
   625	used when the role register is `Role.B`. This is the direct-sum scaffold for the
   626	paper's symmetrized measurements in `inductive_step.tex:55-59`. -/
   627	noncomputable def roleBlock {ιA ιB : Type*}
   628	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) :
   629	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (RoleRegisterLocal ιA ιB) :=
   630	  Matrix.reindex (Equiv.prodComm (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) Role)
   631	    (Equiv.prodComm (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) Role)
   632	    (Matrix.blockDiagonal (roleBlockFamily A B))
   633	
   634	@[simp] theorem roleBlock_A {ιA ιB : Type*}
   635	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB))
   636	    (i j : LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) :
   637	    roleBlock A B (Role.A, i) (Role.A, j) = A i j :=
   638	  rfl
   639	
   640	@[simp] theorem roleBlock_B {ιA ιB : Type*}
   641	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB))
   642	    (i j : LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) :
   643	    roleBlock A B (Role.B, i) (Role.B, j) = B i j :=
   644	  rfl
   645	
   646	@[simp] theorem roleBlock_AB {ιA ιB : Type*}
   647	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB))
   648	    (i j : LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) :
   649	    roleBlock A B (Role.A, i) (Role.B, j) = 0 :=
   650	  rfl
   651	
   652	@[simp] theorem roleBlock_BA {ιA ιB : Type*}
   653	    (A B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB))
   654	    (i j : LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB) :
   655	    roleBlock A B (Role.B, i) (Role.A, j) = 0 :=
   656	  rfl
   657	
   658	@[simp] theorem roleBlock_one {ιA ιB : Type*}
   659	    [DecidableEq ιA] [DecidableEq ιB] :
   660	    roleBlock (1 : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (LocalCarrierSum ιA ιB)) 1 = 1 := by

     3	/-!
     4	# Finite-dimensional state transformations
     5	
     6	This file defines the tensor and reindexing operations used for strategy
     7	distance, Magic Square rigidity, and the qudit-to-qubit isomorphism. See
     8	blueprint chapters 11--13 and the declaration-level references below.
     9	-/
    10	
    11	open scoped Matrix
    12	
    13	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    14	
    15	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    16	
    17	/-- Conjugation by the local isometries in `thm:ms-rigidity` and
    18	`lem:pauli-binary`; blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244` and
    19	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:710-741`, paper
    20	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652` and
    21	`04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. -/
    22	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}
    23	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι']
    24	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    25	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    26	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap
    27	  U * M * Uᴴ
    28	
    29	/-- Coordinate transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    30	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    31	noncomputable def reindexState {ι ι' : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    32	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    33	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    34	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    35	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))
    36	
    37	/-- Apply the two independent local isometries of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    38	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    39	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    40	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    41	    {ιA ιB κA κB : Type*}
    42	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    43	    [Fintype κA] [DecidableEq κA] [Fintype κB] [DecidableEq κB]
    44	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κA)
    45	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ κB)
    46	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)) :
    47	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (κA × κB) :=
    48	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (κA × κB) ℂ).symm
    49	    (fun p =>
    50	      ∑ i : ιA, ∑ j : ιB,
    51	        ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κA ℂ)
    52	            (φA ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιA ℂ).symm (Pi.single i 1))) p.1) *
    53	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv κB ℂ)
    54	            (φB ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ιB ℂ).symm (Pi.single j 1))) p.2) *
    55	          ((EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA × ιB) ℂ) ψ (i, j)))
    56	
    57	/-- Coordinate tensor used in the ideal state of `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    58	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    59	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    60	noncomputable def vecTensor {ι κ : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
    62	    (u : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ κ) :
    63	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ι × κ) :=
    64	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ι × κ) ℂ).symm
    65	    (fun p => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ u) p.1 * (EuclideanSpace.equiv κ ℂ v) p.2)
    66	
    67	/-- Operator transport used by `def:strategy-distance`, blueprint
    68	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    69	def reindexOp {ι ι' : Type*} (e : ι ≃ ι') (M : Op ι') : Op ι :=
    70	  (Matrix.reindex e.symm e.symm) M
    71	
    72	/-- Four-factor tensor shuffle used by `thm:ms-rigidity`; blueprint
    73	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:222-244`, paper
    74	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:620-652`. -/
    75	def prodShuffle {α β γ δ : Type*} :
    76	    (α × β) × (γ × δ) ≃ (α × γ) × (β × δ) where
    77	  toFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    78	  invFun p := ((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2, p.2.2))
    79	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    80	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    81

     7	Core quantum-state definitions together with tensor-placement operators.
     8	-/
     9	
    10	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    11	
    12	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    13	
    14	/-- A PSD density matrix indexed by `ι`.
    15	
    16	There is intentionally no global `Inhabited` instance: the zero matrix is PSD but
    17	not a physical state of unit trace, so an ambient default would silently
    18	trivialize later statements. Use `IsNormalized` to additionally require
    19	`τ(ρ) = 1`.
    20	
    21	This remains the ambient state space for the current LDT development: strategy
    22	packages in `LDT/Test/StrategyCore.lean`, the SWAP-symmetry API `PermInvState`,
    23	and the expectation-value lemmas in `LDT/Basic/OperatorExpectations.lean` are all
    24	stated for arbitrary density matrices, not only pure states. -/
    25	structure QuantumState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] where
    26	  density : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι := 0
    27	  density_psd : 0 ≤ density := by positivity
    28	
    29	/-- Unit normalized trace for the concrete matrix carried by a state. -/
    30	def QuantumState.IsNormalized {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) : Prop :=
    32	  MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 1
    33	
    34	/-- A normalized state has a nonempty carrier: if the carrier were empty, the
    35	trace would vanish and `normalizedTrace = 0 / 0 = 0`, contradicting `= 1`. -/
    36	theorem QuantumState.IsNormalized.nonempty {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	    {ψ : QuantumState ι} (hψ : ψ.IsNormalized) : Nonempty ι := by
    38	  by_contra h
    39	  rw [not_nonempty_iff] at h
    40	  letI := h
    41	  rw [QuantumState.IsNormalized] at hψ
    42	  have hzero : MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 0 := by
    43	    simp [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace]
    44	  exact zero_ne_one (hzero.symm.trans hψ)
    45	
    46	/-- The scaled rank-one density matrix attached to a state vector.
    47	
    48	Because this development uses the normalized trace `τ(A) = tr(A) / dim`, the
    49	quantum state represented by a unit vector `ψ` is `dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|` rather than the
    50	raw projector `|ψ⟩⟨ψ|`. This scaling makes `τ(ρ) = 1` and keeps `ev` aligned
    51	with the paper's bra-ket expectations. -/
    52	noncomputable def pureDensity {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    53	    (ψ : ι → ℂ) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
    54	  (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) • Matrix.vecMulVec ψ (star ψ)
    55	
    56	/-- Swap the two tensor coordinates of a bipartite state vector. -/
    57	def swapVector {ι : Type*} (ψ : ι × ι → ℂ) : ι × ι → ℂ :=
    58	  fun ij => ψ (ij.2, ij.1)
    59	
    60	/-- A pure-state witness as a unit vector in the ambient finite Hilbert space.
    61	
    62	The associated density matrix is `pureDensity ψ.vector = dim · |ψ⟩⟨ψ|`, so that
    63	coercing to `QuantumState` preserves the paper's scalar `⟨ψ|X|ψ⟩` formulas
    64	despite our use of the normalized trace. -/
    65	structure PureState (ι : Type*) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] where
    66	  vector : ι → ℂ
    67	  unit : star vector ⬝ᵥ vector = 1
    68	
    69	namespace PureState
    70	
    71	/-- The coordinate-basis vector has unit self-dot product. -/
    72	private theorem basis_unit {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    73	    (i : ι) :
    74	    star (fun j => if j = i then (1 : ℂ) else 0) ⬝ᵥ
    75	        (fun j => if j = i then (1 : ℂ) else 0) = 1 := by
    76	  rw [dotProduct]
    77	  simp
    78	
    79	/-- The coordinate-basis pure state at a distinguished basis vector. -/
    80	noncomputable def basis {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    81	    (i : ι) : PureState ι where
    82	  vector := fun j => if j = i then 1 else 0
    83	  unit := basis_unit i
    84	
    85	/-- The density matrix represented by a pure-state witness. -/
    86	noncomputable def density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    87	    (ψ : PureState ι) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι :=
    88	  pureDensity ψ.vector
    89	
    90	theorem density_psd {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    91	    (ψ : PureState ι) :
    92	    0 ≤ ψ.density := by
    93	  refine Matrix.nonneg_iff_posSemidef.mpr ?_
    94	  exact (Matrix.posSemidef_vecMulVec_self_star ψ.vector).smul
    95	    (by positivity : 0 ≤ (Fintype.card ι : ℂ))
    96	
    97	noncomputable def toQuantumState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
    98	    (ψ : PureState ι) : QuantumState ι where
    99	  density := ψ.density
   100	  density_psd := ψ.density_psd
   101	
   102	noncomputable instance {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι] :
   103	    Coe (PureState ι) (QuantumState ι) where
   104	  coe := toQuantumState
   105	
   106	@[simp] theorem coe_density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   107	    (ψ : PureState ι) :
   108	    (ψ : QuantumState ι).density = ψ.density := rfl
   109	
   110	theorem normalizedTrace_density {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   111	    (ψ : PureState ι) :
   112	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ψ.density = 1 := by
   113	  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   114	  unfold density pureDensity MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   115	  rw [Matrix.trace_smul, Matrix.trace_vecMulVec, dotProduct_comm, ψ.unit]
   116	  change ((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) * 1) / (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) = 1
   117	  rw [mul_one, div_self hcard]
   118	
   119	theorem toQuantumState_isNormalized {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   120	    (ψ : PureState ι) :
   121	    (ψ : QuantumState ι).IsNormalized := by
   122	  simpa [QuantumState.IsNormalized] using ψ.normalizedTrace_density
   123	
   124	theorem normalizedTrace_density_mul {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   125	    (ψ : PureState ι) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
   126	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X) =
   127	      star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) := by
   128	  have hcard : (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) ≠ 0 := Nat.cast_ne_zero.mpr Fintype.card_ne_zero
   129	  calc
   130	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace ((ψ : QuantumState ι).density * X)
   131	      = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * (ψ : QuantumState ι).density) := by
   132	          rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_mul_comm]
   133	    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * ψ.density) := by rfl
   134	    _ = MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace
   135	          ((Fintype.card ι : ℂ) • (X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector))) := by
   136	          simp [density, pureDensity]
   137	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   138	          MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector)) := by
   139	          rw [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace_smul]
   140	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   141	          (((X * Matrix.vecMulVec ψ.vector (star ψ.vector)).trace) /
   142	            (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
   143	          simp [MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace]
   144	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   145	          (((Matrix.vecMulVec (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) (star ψ.vector)).trace) /
   146	            (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
   147	          rw [Matrix.mul_vecMulVec]
   148	    _ = (Fintype.card ι : ℂ) *
   149	          (((X *ᵥ ψ.vector) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.vector) / (Fintype.card ι : ℂ)) := by
   150	          rw [Matrix.trace_vecMulVec]
   151	    _ = (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) ⬝ᵥ star ψ.vector := by
   152	          field_simp [hcard]
   153	    _ = star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector) := by
   154	          rw [dotProduct_comm]
   155	
   156	/-- Vector-level SWAP invariance for a bipartite pure-state witness.
   157	
   158	This is stronger than density-level SWAP invariance: it records the paper's
   159	honest vector symmetry and rules out antisymmetric vectors, even though those
   160	vectors define SWAP-invariant density matrices. -/
   161	def IsSwapInvariant {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   162	    (ψ : PureState (ι × ι)) : Prop :=
   163	  swapVector ψ.vector = ψ.vector
   164	
   165	end PureState
   166	
   167	@[simp] theorem swapVector_swapVector {ι : Type*} (ψ : ι × ι → ℂ) :
   168	    swapVector (swapVector ψ) = ψ := by
   169	  funext ij
   170	  rcases ij with ⟨i, j⟩
   171	  rfl
   172	
   173	/-- The expectation `Re τ(ψ X)`. Dimensions match by construction. -/
   174	noncomputable def ev {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   175	    (ψ : QuantumState ι) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) : Error :=
   176	  Complex.re <| MIPStarRE.Quantum.normalizedTrace (ψ.density * X)
   177	
   178	theorem PureState.ev_eq_re_inner {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] [Nonempty ι]
   179	    (ψ : PureState ι) (X : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι) :
   180	    ev (ψ : QuantumState ι) X =
   181	      Complex.re (star ψ.vector ⬝ᵥ (X *ᵥ ψ.vector)) := by
   182	  unfold ev
   183	  rw [ψ.normalizedTrace_density_mul]
   184	
   185	/-- Tensor product of two operators via Kronecker product. -/
   186	abbrev opTensor {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   187	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) :
   188	    MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι₁ × ι₂) :=
   189	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   190	
   191	/-- Left placement `A ⊗ I` on a bipartite space `ι₁ × ι₂`. -/
   192	abbrev leftTensor {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   193	    (A : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₁) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι₁ × ι₂) :=
   194	  Matrix.kronecker A 1
   195	
   196	/-- Right placement `I ⊗ B` on a bipartite space `ι₁ × ι₂`. -/
   197	abbrev rightTensor {ι₁ ι₂ : Type*} [Fintype ι₁] [DecidableEq ι₁] [Fintype ι₂] [DecidableEq ι₂]
   198	    (B : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op ι₂) : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (ι₁ × ι₂) :=
   199	  Matrix.kronecker 1 B
   200

     3	/-!
     4	# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project
     5	
     6	This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.
     7	
     8	## Main definitions
     9	
    10	* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
    11	* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
    12	* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
    13	* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
    14	* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
    15	* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
    20	the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
    21	for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    25	
    26	namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/
    29	
    30	/--
    31	A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
    32	`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
    33	-/
    34	structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
    35	  /-- The effect operators. -/
    36	  effect : α → Op d
    37	  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
    38	  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
    39	  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
    40	  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1
    41	
    42	/--
    43	A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
    44	-/
    45	structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    46	    extends Submeasurement α d where
    47	  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
    48	  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1
    49	
    50	/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/
    51	
    52	namespace Submeasurement
    53	
    54	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    55	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    56	
    57	/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/
    58	
    59	/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
    60	noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
    61	  ∑ a, M.effect a
    62	
    63	/--
    64	Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
    65	fibers.
    66	-/
    67	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    68	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
    69	  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    70	  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
    71	  sum_le_one := by
    72	    calc
    73	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
    74	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
    75	      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one
    76	
    77	/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
    78	theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    79	    M.total ≤ 1 := by
    80	  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one
    81	
    82	/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
    83	theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    84	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    85	    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
    86	  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm
    87	
    88	/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
    89	theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    90	    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    91	    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
    92	  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm
    93	
    94	end Submeasurement
    95	
    96	namespace Measurement
    97	
    98	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    99	variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
   100	
   101	/--
   102	Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.
   103	
   104	This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
   105	the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
   106	sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
   107	-/
   108	def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
   109	    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
   110	  effect := effect
   111	  pos := pos
   112	  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
   113	  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one
   114	
   115	/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
   116	theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
   117	    M.total = 1 :=
   118	  M.sum_eq_one
   119	
   120	/--
   121	Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.
   122	
   123	This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
   124	the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
   125	remains a POVM after postprocessing.
   126	-/
   127	noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   128	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
   129	  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
   130	  sum_eq_one := by
   131	    calc
   132	      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
   133	          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
   134	      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one
   135	
   136	@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   137	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
   138	    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
   139	      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
   140	  rfl
   141	
   142	@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
   143	    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
   144	    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
   145	  rfl
   146	
   147	end Measurement
   148	
   149	/-! ## Overlap definitions -/
   150	
   151	section Overlap
   152	
   153	variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
   154	variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
   155	
   156	/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   158	  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)
   159	
   160	/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
   161	noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
   162	  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)
   163	
   164	end Overlap
   165	
   166	end MIPStarRE.Quantum

     4	/-!
     5	# The quantum linearity theorem
     6	
     7	This file states the external quantum-linearity result used to combine the
     8	binary observables produced in the point analysis.  The statement uses a
     9	positive semidefinite trace-one operator, and its conclusion adjoins a finite ancillary
    10	space on which the exactly linear observables act.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The declaration is `thm:linearity` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`.  The quotation in the
    16	QPBT paper is at
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`; the
    18	provider is Theorem 10 of Natarajan--Vidick, arXiv:1610.03574.
    19	-/
    20	
    21	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    22	
    23	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    24	
    25	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    26	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    27	
    28	noncomputable section
    29	
    30	/-- A binary observable is a Hermitian operator whose square is the identity.
    31	This is the finite-matrix realization of `Obs(H)` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    32	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`, quoted at paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`. -/
    34	def IsBinaryObservable {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    35	    (O : Op ι) : Prop :=
    36	  O.IsHermitian ∧ O * O = 1
    37	
    38	/-- The rank-one density operator associated with an ancillary vector. -/
    39	noncomputable def ancProj {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    40	    (v : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : Op ι :=
    41	  let w := (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) v
    42	  Matrix.vecMulVec w (star w)
    43	
    44	/-- Squared state-dependent distance between two operators.  This is the
    45	quantity `d_rho(S,T)^2` in `thm:linearity`, blueprint
    46	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-180`. -/
    47	noncomputable def stateDepDistSq {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    48	    (S T ρ : Op ι) : ℝ :=
    49	  (Matrix.trace ((S - T)ᴴ * (S - T) * ρ)).re
    50	
    51	/-- The quantum linearity theorem imported from Natarajan--Vidick.
    52	
    53	The statement is `thm:linearity` in
    54	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:82-145`; the QPBT paper quotes
    55	it at
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:713-725`.
    57	
    58	As recorded in `rem:linearity-import` (blueprint lines 147--180), this
    59	provider-faithful form imposes no upper bound on `δ`, preserves the error,
    60	asserts exact linearity for every pair, and averages closeness only over `u`.
    61	The paper quotation instead adds `δ ≤ 1`, phrases closeness pointwise under a
    62	pair quantifier, and appends `L 0 = 1`; those three deviations are not
    63	reproduced.  The identity at zero follows later from exact linearity and the
    64	binary-observable condition. -/
    65	theorem exists_exactly_linear_observables {ι : Type}
    66	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    67	    (t : ℕ) (ht : 0 < t) (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    68	    (ρ : Op ι) (hρ : ρ.PosSemidef) (htrace : ρ.trace = 1)
    69	    (O : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op ι)
    70	    (hO : ∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (O u))
    71	    (hcorrelation :
    72	      1 - δ ≤ avgOver
    73	        (uniformDistribution
    74	          ((Fin t → ZMod 2) × (Fin t → ZMod 2)))
    75	        (fun pair =>
    76	          (Matrix.trace
    77	            (O pair.1 * O pair.2 * O (pair.1 + pair.2) * ρ)).re)) :
    78	    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (_ : DecidableEq ι')
    79	        (anc : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι'),
    80	      ‖anc‖ = 1 ∧
    81	        ∃ L : (Fin t → ZMod 2) → Op (ι × ι'),
    82	          (∀ u, IsBinaryObservable (L u)) ∧

   482	      instField := inferInstance
   483	      instFintype := inferInstance
   484	      instDecidableEq := inferInstance
   485	      equiv := fieldEquiv

   492	    representation_natural := ?_

   494	    normal := ?_

   498	    simp only [fieldEquiv, Equiv.trans_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_toEquiv,
   499	      LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply, bitEquiv]

   502	    intro i _

    16	/-- A coded function has low individual degree when it is represented by an actual
    17	multivariate polynomial over the chosen field model whose degree in each variable is at
    18	most `d`. -/
    19	def HasLowIndividualDegree (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    20	    (g : Point params → Fq params) : Prop :=
    21	  ∃ p : PolynomialModel params,
    22	    (∀ i, MvPolynomial.degreeOf i p ≤ params.d) ∧
    23	      g = evalPolynomialModel params p
    24	
    25	/-- A coded univariate function has degree at most `bound` when it is represented by
    26	an actual polynomial over the chosen field model of degree at most `bound`. -/
    27	def HasUnivariateDegreeAtMost (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    28	    (bound : ℕ) (f : Fq params → Fq params) : Prop :=
    29	  ∃ p : LinePolynomialModel params,
    30	    p.natDegree ≤ bound ∧
    31	      f = evalLinePolynomialModel params p

    33	/-- Composing with the degree-one translation `C a + X` preserves `natDegree`

    36	theorem natDegree_comp_C_add_X_le {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    37	    (p : LinePolynomialModel params) (a : Scalar params) {n : ℕ}
    38	    (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n) :
    39	    (p.comp (_root_.Polynomial.C a + _root_.Polynomial.X)).natDegree ≤ n :=
    40	  le_trans (_root_.Polynomial.natDegree_comp_le)
    41	    (by rw [add_comm, _root_.Polynomial.natDegree_X_add_C, Nat.mul_one]; exact hp)

     3	/-!

     5	
     6	Diagonal-line geometry and rebasing operations.
     7	
     8	## References
     9	
    10	- `references/ldt-paper/test_definition.tex`
    11	- `blueprint/src/chapter/ch02_test.tex`
    12	-/
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    15	
    16	/-- A genuinely affine diagonal line in `F_q^m`. -/
    17	structure DiagonalLine (params : Parameters) where
    18	  base : Point params
    19	  direction : Point params
    20	
    21	deriving instance DecidableEq, Inhabited for DiagonalLine
    22	
    23	namespace DiagonalLine
    24	
    25	/-- The canonical affine parameterization `t ↦ base + t · direction`. -/
    26	def pointAt {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    27	    (ℓ : DiagonalLine params) : Fq params → Point params :=
    28	  fun t => addPoint ℓ.base (smulPoint t ℓ.direction)
    29	
    30	/-- The support of the nonzero coordinates of a direction vector. -/
    31	noncomputable def nonzeroDirectionSupport {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    32	    (v : Point params) : Finset (Fin params.m) :=
    33	  Finset.univ.filter fun i => v i ≠ zeroCoord
    34	
    35	/-- The least nonzero coordinate of a direction vector, when one exists. -/
    36	noncomputable def firstNonzeroCoord? {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    37	    (v : Point params) : Option (Fin params.m) :=
    38	  open Classical in
    39	  let s := nonzeroDirectionSupport (params := params) v
    40	  if hs : s.Nonempty then some (s.min' hs) else none
    41	
    42	/-- Normalize a direction vector so its first nonzero coordinate becomes `1`. -/
    43	noncomputable def normalizeDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    44	    (v : Point params) : Point params :=
    45	  open Classical in
    46	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    47	    | none => zeroPoint
    48	    | some i => smulPoint (invCoord (v i)) v
    49	
    50	/-- Canonical geometric diagonal line through `u` in direction `v`.
    51	
    52	For nonzero `v`, we normalize by the first nonzero coordinate and shift the
    53	base point so that this pivot coordinate is `0`. The degenerate `v = 0` case is
    54	kept as the singleton line through `u`. -/
    55	noncomputable def throughPointDirection {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    56	    (u v : Point params) : DiagonalLine params :=
    57	  open Classical in
    58	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    59	    | none => { base := u, direction := zeroPoint }
    60	    | some i =>
    61	        let w := normalizeDirection (params := params) v
    62	        let t := u i
    63	        { base := fun j => subCoord (u j) (mulCoord t (w j))
    64	          direction := w }
    65	
    66	/-- Affine parameter of the sampled point on the canonical diagonal line through
    67	`u` in direction `v`. -/
    68	noncomputable def sampleParameter {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    69	    (u v : Point params) : Fq params :=
    70	  open Classical in
    71	  match firstNonzeroCoord? (params := params) v with
    72	    | none => zeroCoord
    73	    | some i => u i
    74

     3	/-!
     4	# Lines and canonical representatives
     5	
     6	The classical and Pauli question distributions use affine lines in a finite
     7	coordinate space.  This module keeps the zero-direction case explicit and
     8	provides the canonical projection used for line representatives.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	The source-facing nodes are `def:line`, `prop:line-equiv`, and
    13	`def:line-representative` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:433-492`.
    14	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:102-174`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	variable {K : Type*} [Field K]
    22	
    23	/--
    24	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    25	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`;
    26	paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    28	-/
    29	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    30	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    31	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}
    32	
    33	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    34	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    36	-/
    37	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    38	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    39	  Pi.single i 1
    40	
    41	/--
    42	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is
    43	the axis-parallel clause of `def:line` (blueprint lines 445-450; paper
    44	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`).
    45	-/
    46	def IsAxisParallel {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    47	  ∃ i : Fin m, v = coordinateDirection i
    48	
    49	/--
    50	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may
    51	vanish.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:439-453`; paper origin
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    53	-/
    54	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    55	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0
    56	
    57	/--
    58	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    59	This is `prop:line-equiv` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:455-466`,
    60	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.
    61	-/
    62	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    63	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    64	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    65	  sorry
    66	
    67	/--
    68	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    69	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    70	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,
    71	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`; paper origin
    72	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:143-174`.
    73	-/
    74	noncomputable def lineRepMap {m : ℕ}
    75	    (v : Fin m → K) : (Fin m → K) →ₗ[K] (Fin m → K) :=
    76	  canonicalProjOfKernel (Submodule.span K ({v} : Set (Fin m → K)))
    77	
    78	/- The point-valued companion to `lineRepMap`; Lean-only notation for the
    79	canonical representative in `def:line-representative`. -/
    80	/-- The canonical representative point `lineRepMap v u`.  Blueprint
    81	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:472-492`, paper origin
    82	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:166-174`.
    83	-/
    84	noncomputable def lineRep {m : ℕ}
    85	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Fin m → K :=
    86	  lineRepMap v u
    87	
    88	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   106	/-- The successor test obtained by appending one coordinate. -/
   107	def Parameters.next (params : Parameters) : Parameters :=

   109	    q := params.q

   117	/-- The predecessor parameters obtained by removing the last coordinate from a
   118	non-base ambient dimension.
   119	
   120	This is the inverse construction to `Parameters.next` on the data fields.  The
   121	proof fields are inherited from the original parameter bundle, so the inverse is
   122	propositional rather than definitional. -/
   123	def previous (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) : Parameters :=
   124	  { m := params.m - 1
   125	    q := params.q
   126	    d := params.d
   127	    hm := Nat.sub_pos_of_lt hm
   128	    hq := params.hq
   129	    hqPrimePower := params.hqPrimePower }
   130	
   131	/-- Removing the last coordinate and then applying `Parameters.next` recovers the
   132	original non-base parameters. -/
   133	theorem previous_next_eq (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
   134	    (previous params hm).next = params := by
   135	  cases params with
   136	  | mk m q d hm0 hq hqPrimePower =>
   137	      have hsub : m - 1 + 1 = m := Nat.sub_add_cancel (le_of_lt hm)
   138	      simp [previous, Parameters.next, hsub]

   140	/-- A bundled predecessor for a parameter set known to be a successor dimension. -/
   141	structure SuccessorDecomposition (params : Parameters) where
   142	  /-- The predecessor parameter bundle. -/
   143	  pred : Parameters
   144	  /-- The predecessor's successor is the original parameter bundle. -/
   145	  next_eq : pred.next = params
   146	
   147	/-- Every parameter bundle of dimension strictly larger than one has a bundled
   148	predecessor whose successor is propositionally equal to the original bundle. -/
   149	def successorDecompositionOfOneLtM (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
   150	    SuccessorDecomposition params where
   151	  pred := previous params hm
   152	  next_eq := previous_next_eq params hm
   153	
   154	/-- A positive dimension that is not the base dimension is strictly larger than
   155	one. -/
   156	theorem one_lt_m_of_ne_one (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :
   157	    1 < params.m :=
   158	  lt_of_le_of_ne params.hm (Ne.symm hm_ne_one)
   159	
   160	/-- Non-base parameters have a bundled predecessor decomposition. -/
   161	def successorDecompositionOfNeOne (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :
   162	    SuccessorDecomposition params :=
   163	  successorDecompositionOfOneLtM params (one_lt_m_of_ne_one params hm_ne_one)

   224	/-- The carrier bundled in a `FieldModel q` has exactly `q` elements, matching the

   226	@[simp] theorem card (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :

   230	/-- A bundled field model has a nonempty finite carrier. -/
   231	theorem card_pos (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :
   232	    0 < Fintype.card (FieldModel.K q) :=
   233	  Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨0⟩

   235	/-- The finite cardinality of a bundled field model is nonzero. -/
   236	theorem card_ne_zero (q : ℕ) [FieldModel q] :
   237	    Fintype.card (FieldModel.K q) ≠ 0 :=

   242	/-- Build the honest field model from prime-power data. -/
   243	@[reducible] noncomputable def PrimePowerFieldSpec.toFieldModel (params : Parameters)
   244	    (spec : PrimePowerFieldSpec params) : FieldModel params.q := by
   245	  classical
   246	  letI : Fact spec.p.Prime := ⟨spec.pPrime⟩
   247	  let K := HonestFq params spec
   248	  letI : Fintype K := Fintype.ofFinite K
   249	  have hcard : Fintype.card K = params.q := by
   250	    rw [← Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, spec.cardEq]
   251	    simpa [K, HonestFq] using (GaloisField.card (p := spec.p) (n := spec.n) spec.nPos.ne')
   252	  exact
   253	    { K := K
   254	      instField := inferInstance
   255	      instFintype := inferInstance
   256	      instDecidableEq := inferInstance
   257	      equiv := Fintype.equivFinOfCardEq hcard }

1	\section{The test}\label{sec:the-test}
     2	
     3	\begin{definition}[Roles]
     4	The low individual degree test will be played between two provers and a verifier.
     5	The two provers are named Player~$\mathrm{A}$ and Player~$\mathrm{B}$.
     6	A \emph{role} $r$ is an element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$.
     7	Given a role~$r$, we write $\overline{r}$ for the other element of the set $\{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$.
     8	\end{definition}
     9	
    10	\begin{definition}[Low individual degree test]
    11	Let~$m$ and~$d$ be nonnegative integers.
    12	Let $q$ be a prime power.
    13	Then the \emph{$(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test}
    14	is stated in \Cref{fig:test}.
    15	\end{definition}
    16	
    17	{
    18	\floatstyle{boxed} 
    19	\restylefloat{figure}
    20	\begin{figure}
    21	With probability~$\tfrac{1}{3}$ each, perform one of the following three tests.
    22	\begin{enumerate}
    23		\item \textbf{Axis-parallel lines test:}
    24			Pick a uniformly random role $\br \sim \{\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\}$.
    25			Let $\bu \sim \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point.
    26			Select $\bi \sim \{1, \ldots, m\}$ uniformly at random,
    27			and let $\bell = \{\bu + t \cdot e_{\bi} \mid t \in \F_q\}$
    28			be the axis-parallel line which passes through~$\bu$ in the $\bi$-th direction.
    29			\begin{itemize}
    30			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\br$: 
    31				Give $\bell$;
    32				receive the univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $\boldf:\bell \rightarrow \F_q$.
    33			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\overline{\br}$:
    34				Give $\bu$;
    35				receive $\ba \in \F_q$.
    36			\end{itemize}
    37			Accept if $\boldf(\bu) = \ba$.
    38		\item \textbf{Self-consistency test:}
    39			Let $\bu \sim \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point.
    40			\begin{itemize}
    41			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\mathrm{A}$: 
    42				Give $\bu$;
    43				receive $\ba \in \F_q$.
    44			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\mathrm{B}$:
    45				Give $\bu$;
    46				receive $\bb \in \F_q$.
    47			\end{itemize}
    48			Accept if $\ba = \bb$.
    49		\item \textbf{Diagonal lines test:}
    50			Pick a uniformly random role $\br \sim \{\mathrm{A},\mathrm{B}\}$.
    51			Let $\bu \sim \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point.
    52			Select $\bi \sim \{1, \ldots, m\}$ uniformly at random,
    53			and let $\bv \in \F_q^m$ be a uniformly random point whose last $m - \bi$ coordinates are~$0$.
    54			Finally,
    55			let $\bell = \{\bu + t \cdot \bv \mid t \in \F_q\}$
    56			be the line which passes through~$\bu$ in direction~$\bv$.
    57			\begin{itemize}
    58			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\br$: 
    59				Give $\bell$;
    60				receive the univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $\boldf:\bell \rightarrow \F_q$.
    61			\item[$\circ$] Player~$\overline{\br}$:
    62				Give $\bu$;
    63				receive $\ba \in \F_q$.
    64			\end{itemize}
    65			Accept if $\boldf(\bu) = \ba$.
    66		\end{enumerate}
    67		\caption{The $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.\label{fig:test}}
    68	\end{figure}
    69	}
    70	
    71	An important class of strategies are those which are \emph{symmetric}.
    72	In this case, the bipartite state $\ket{\psi}$ Alice and Bob share is symmetric.
    73	Furthermore, for any question Alice and Bob receive, they apply the same measurement to their share of the state.
    74	This means that rather than, for example, keeping track of a separate points measurement for Alice and Bob,
    75	we can use a single measurement to refer to both of their strategies,
    76	and similarly for the axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines measurements.
    77	This is formalized in the following definition, where we also consider strategies which are projective.
    78	
    79	\begin{definition}[Symmetric, projective strategy]
    80	A \emph{symmetric, projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
    81	is a tuple $(\psi, A, B, L)$ defined as follows.
    82	\begin{itemize}
    83	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH \ot \calH$ is a bipartite, permutation-invariant state.
    84	\item[$\circ$] $A = \{A^u_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
    85				For each $u$, $A^u$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    86	\item[$\circ$] $B = \{B^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    87				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    88				For each $\ell$, $B^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    89	\item[$\circ$] $L = \{L^{\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
    90				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
    91				For each $\ell$, $L^{\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH$.
    92	\end{itemize}
    93	\end{definition}
    94	
    95	We can also consider more general strategies which are no longer assumed to be symmetric.
    96	In this case, Players~$\mathrm{A}$ and~$\mathrm{B}$ each have their own versions of the measurements~$A$, $B$, and~$L$.
    97	
    98	\begin{definition}[General projective strategy]
    99	A \emph{projective strategy} for the $(m,q, d)$-low individual degree test
   100	is a tuple $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ defined as follows.
   101	\begin{itemize}
   102	\item[$\circ$] $\ket{\psi} \in \calH_{\mathrm{A}} \ot \calH_{\mathrm{B}}$ is a bipartite state.
   103	\end{itemize}
   104	Furthermore, for each~$w \in \{\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}\}$:
   105	\begin{itemize}
   106	\item[$\circ$] $A^{w} = \{A^{w,u}_a\}$ contains a matrix for each $u \in \F_q^m$ and $a \in \F_q$.
   107				For each $u$, $A^{w,u}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   108	\item[$\circ$] $B^{w} = \{B^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each axis-parallel line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   109				and univariate degree-$d$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   110				For each $\ell$, $B^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   111	\item[$\circ$] $L^w = \{L^{w,\ell}_f\}$ contains a matrix for each line~$\ell$ in $\F_q^m$
   112				and univariate degree-$md$ polynomial $f:\ell\rightarrow \F_q$.
   113				For each $\ell$, $L^{w,\ell}$ is a projective measurement on~$\calH_{w}$.
   114	\end{itemize}
   115	\end{definition}
   116	
   117	\begin{remark}
   118	Throughout this work, we will only consider projective strategies.
   119	So we will henceforth use the terms ``strategy" and ``symmetric strategy'' to refer exclusively to projective strategies and symmetric, projective strategies, respectively.
   120	
   121	In addition, we will spend the vast majority of this work dealing solely with symmetric strategies, as they are notationally simpler to work with.
   122	Much of this work will focus on proving~\Cref{thm:main-induction},
   123	a variant of our main theorem for symmetric strategies.
   124	Our main theorem for general strategies, \Cref{thm:main-formal} below, will be proven in \Cref{sec:induction} by a standard reduction to the symmetric case.
   125	We will only see these more cumbersome-to-write general strategies
   126	in this section, where we state \Cref{thm:main-formal},
   127	and in \Cref{sec:induction}, where we carry out the reduction.
   128	\end{remark}
   129	
   130	\begin{definition}[Good strategy]
   131	A strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good if it
   132	passes the axis-parallel lines test with probability at least $1-\eps$,
   133	the self consistency test with probability at least~$1-\delta$,
   134	and the diagonal lines test with probability at least~$1-\gamma$.
   135	\end{definition}
   136	
   137	\begin{remark}\label{rem:good-strat-characterization}
   138	Using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:comparing-measurements} below,
   139	a symmetric strategy is $(\eps, \delta, \gamma)$-good
   140	if and only if it satisfies the following three conditions.
   141	For $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the axis-parallel lines test,
   142	\begin{equation*}
   143	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\eps} I \ot B^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]},
   144	\quad
   145	\text{and}
   146	\quad
   147	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\delta} I \ot A^u_a.
   148	\end{equation*}
   149	And for $\bell$ and $\bu$ as in the diagonal lines test,
   150	\begin{equation*}
   151	A^u_a \ot I \simeq_{\gamma} I \ot L^{\ell}_{[f(u)=a]}.
   152	\end{equation*}
   153	\end{remark}
   154	
   155	\begin{notation}\label{not:conditioned-on-last-direction}
   156	Our proof will be via induction,
   157	i.e.\ proving soundness of the $(m+1,q,d)$-low individual degree test
   158	using the soundness of the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   159	To do this, we will frequently use the axis-parallel line test in the specific case of $i = m+1$.
   160	Thus, it will be convenient to introduce the following notation.
   161	Let $(\psi, A, B, L)$ be a symmetric strategy for the $(m+1, q, d)$-low individual degree test,
   162	Then for each $u \in \F_q^m$ we will write $B^u_f$ as shorthand for $B^{\ell}_f$,
   163	where $\ell = \{(u, x) \mid x \in \F_q\}$.
   164	For a function $f:\ell \rightarrow \F_q$,
   165	we will also sometimes write $f(x)$ as shorthand for $f(u,x)$.
   166	\end{notation}
   167	
   168	\begin{definition}
   169	Consider the $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test.
   170	For $j \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$,
   171	we refer to the \emph{$j$-restricted diagonal lines test}
   172	as the diagonal lines test conditioned on $\bi = j$.
   173	For example, in the $m$-restricted diagonal lines test,
   174	the line $\bell$ is simply a uniformly random line in $\F_q^m$.
   175	\end{definition}
   176	
   177	Now we state our main theorem using notation which will be introduced in \Cref{sec:prelims} below.
   178	This the formal version of \Cref{thm:main-informal}.
   179	
   180	\begin{theorem}[Main theorem; quantum soundness of the low individual degree test]\label{thm:main-formal}
   181	  Consider a projective strategy $(\psi, A^{\mathrm{A}},B^{\mathrm{A}},L^{\mathrm{A}},A^{\mathrm{B}},B^{\mathrm{B}},L^{\mathrm{B}})$ 
   182	   which passes the  $(m,q,d)$-low individual degree test with probability at least $1-\eps$.
   183	  Let $k \geq md$ be an integer.
   184	  Let
   185	  \begin{equation*}
   186	  \nu = 100000 k^2m^4 \cdot \Big(\eps^{1/40000} + (d/q)^{1/40000} + e^{-k/(2560000m^2)}\Big).
   187	  \end{equation*}
   188	Then there exists projective measurements $G^{\mathrm{A}}, G^{\mathrm{B}} \in \polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ with the following properties:
   189	\begin{enumerate}
   190	  \item (Consistency with~$A$):  On average over $\bu \sim \F_q^{m}$,
   191		  \begin{align*}
   192		  A^{\mathrm{A},u}_a \otimes I
   193		  	&\simeq_{\nu} I \otimes G^{\mathrm{B}}_{[g(u)=a]},\\
   194		I \otimes A^{\mathrm{B},u}_a
   195		  	&\simeq_{\nu}  G^{\mathrm{A}}_{[g(u)=a]} \ot I.
   196		  \end{align*}
   197	\item (Self-consistency):
   198		\begin{equation*}
   199		G^{\mathrm{A}}_g \ot I \simeq_{\nu} I \ot G^{\mathrm{B}}_g.
   200		\end{equation*}
   201	\end{enumerate}
   202	\end{theorem}
   203	
   204	We note that there is a tradeoff in \Cref{thm:main-formal} specified by the parameter~$k$.
   205	As~$k$ increases, $\nu$'s prefactor $k^2$ increases.
   206	On the other hand, as $k$ increases, the term $e^{- k/(2560000m^2)}$ which also occurs in $\nu$ \emph{decreases}.
   207	Thus, when applying this theorem, one must select~$k$ to balance these competing demands.
   208	Typically, choosing $k = \poly(m)$ should be more than sufficient for applications.
   209	We believe that this parameter~$k$ is an artifact of our proof,
   210	and we hope that it will be removed in the future.

     3	/-!
     4	# Symmetrized-strategy failure probabilities and test bounds
     5	
     6	Failure-probability surrogates and basic low-individual-degree test bounds for
     7	the split strategy interface.
     8	-/
     9	
    10	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    13	
    14	/-! ### Symmetrized strategies and tested-branch bounds -/
    15	
    16	namespace SymStrat
    17	
    18	/-- Trace-based failure surrogate for the axis-parallel lines test.
    19	Point answers on the left register, line answers (evaluated at the
    20	base point) on the right register of the bipartite state. -/
    21	noncomputable def axisParallelFailureProbability
    22	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    23	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    24	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι) : Error :=
    25	  bipartiteConsError strategy.state
    26	    (uniformDistribution (AxisParallelTestSample params))
    27	    (axisParallelPointAnswerFamily strategy)
    28	    (axisParallelLineAnswerFamily strategy)
    29	
    30	/-- Trace-based failure surrogate for the self-consistency test.
    31	Uses bipartite SSC defect (cross-register overlap).
    32	For projective measurements this equals `bipartiteConsError`
    33	between the same measurement on both registers. -/
    34	noncomputable def selfConsistencyFailureProbability
    35	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    36	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι) : Error :=
    38	  bipartiteSSCError strategy.state
    39	    (uniformDistribution (Point params))
    40	    (IdxProjMeas.toIdxSubMeas strategy.pointMeasurement)
    41	
    42	/-- Trace-based failure surrogate for the diagonal lines test.
    43	Averages over the restriction index `j ∈ {0, …, m − 1}`, then
    44	over the `j`-restricted diagonal test. For each `j`, direction
    45	vectors have the last `m − j − 1` coordinates equal to zero. -/
    46	noncomputable def diagonalFailureProbability
    47	    {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]
    48	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    49	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι) : Error :=
    50	  -- `params.hm : 0 < params.m` ensures the averaging denominator is nonzero.
    51	  (1 / (params.m : Error)) *
    52	    ∑ j : Fin params.m,
    53	      bipartiteConsError strategy.state
    54	        (uniformDistribution
    55	          (RestrictedDiagonalSample params j))
    56	        (diagonalPointAnswerFamily strategy j)
    57	        (diagonalLineAnswerFamily strategy j)
    58	
    59	/-- The paper's notion of an `(ε,δ,γ)`-good symmetric strategy.
    60	
    61	Matches the paper's Definition 3.1: three test-passing bounds with no
    62	extra hypotheses.  The reparametrization covariance that was formerly
    63	listed here is now a structural property of `SymStrat`, where it
    64	belongs (the paper treats diagonal measurements as geometrically
    65	covariant by construction). -/
    66	structure IsGood {params : Parameters} {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    67	    [FieldModel params.q]
    68	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
    69	    (eps delta gamma : Error) : Prop where
    70	  axisParallelTest : strategy.axisParallelFailureProbability ≤ eps
    71	  selfConsistencyTest : strategy.selfConsistencyFailureProbability ≤ delta
    72	  diagonalLineTest : strategy.diagonalFailureProbability ≤ gamma
    73	
    74	end SymStrat
    75	
    76	/-- The diagonal-line failure surrogate is nonnegative. -/
    77	theorem diagonalFailureProbability_nonneg
    78	    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    79	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    80	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι) :
    81	    0 ≤ strategy.diagonalFailureProbability := by
    82	  unfold SymStrat.diagonalFailureProbability
    83	  refine mul_nonneg ?_ ?_
    84	  · positivity
    85	  · refine Finset.sum_nonneg ?_
    86	    intro j _
    87	    exact bipartiteConsError_nonneg strategy.state
    88	      (uniformDistribution (RestrictedDiagonalSample params j))
    89	      (diagonalPointAnswerFamily strategy j)
    90	      (diagonalLineAnswerFamily strategy j)
    91	
    92	/-- A good symmetric strategy has a nonnegative axis-parallel error parameter
    93	`ε`. -/
    94	theorem eps_nonneg_of_isGood
    95	    (params : Parameters)
    96	    [FieldModel params.q]
    97	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    98	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
    99	    {eps delta gamma : Error}
   100	    (hgood : strategy.IsGood eps delta gamma) :
   101	    0 ≤ eps := by
   102	  exact le_trans
   103	    (bipartiteConsError_nonneg strategy.state
   104	      (uniformDistribution (AxisParallelTestSample params))
   105	      (axisParallelPointAnswerFamily strategy)
   106	      (axisParallelLineAnswerFamily strategy))
   107	    hgood.axisParallelTest
   108	
   109	/-- A good symmetric strategy has a nonnegative self-consistency error
   110	parameter `δ`. -/
   111	theorem delta_nonneg_of_isGood
   112	    (params : Parameters)
   113	    [FieldModel params.q]
   114	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   115	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
   116	    {eps delta gamma : Error}
   117	    (hgood : strategy.IsGood eps delta gamma) :
   118	    0 ≤ delta := by

   121	      (uniformDistribution (Point params))

   123	    hgood.selfConsistencyTest
   124	
   125	/-- A good symmetric strategy has a nonnegative diagonal-lines error parameter
   126	`γ`. -/
   127	theorem gamma_nonneg_of_isGood
   128	    (params : Parameters)
   129	    [FieldModel params.q]
   130	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   131	    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)
   132	    {eps delta gamma : Error}
   133	    (hgood : strategy.IsGood eps delta gamma) :
   134	    0 ≤ gamma := by
   135	  exact le_trans (diagonalFailureProbability_nonneg params strategy)
   136	    hgood.diagonalLineTest

   177	    [FieldModel params.q]

   193	    [FieldModel params.q]
   194	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]

   202	/-- If three nonnegative summands have average at most `eps`, each summand is at

import Mathlib

/-!
# Basic finite-dimensional matrix operators

This module contains the elementary trace and matrix-algebra facts used by the
finite-dimensional quantum layer.  It introduces the local operator abbreviation
`Op d = Matrix d d ℂ` and keeps the basic trace bookkeeping independent of the
positive-semidefinite order and normalized-trace material.

## References

The declarations in this file are matrix facts for the LDT
formalization of `references/ldt-paper/`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder Matrix.Norms.Elementwise
open WithLp

namespace Matrix

/-! ### Trace bookkeeping -/

/-- Reindexing rows and columns by the same equivalence preserves matrix trace.

This generic matrix lemma is used when moving between equivalent finite index
presentations of the same operator. -/
theorem trace_reindex {α β R : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]
    [AddCommMonoid R] (e : α ≃ β) (M : Matrix α α R) :
    Matrix.trace (Matrix.reindex e e M) = Matrix.trace M := by
  classical
  simp only [Matrix.trace, Matrix.diag_apply, Matrix.reindex_apply]
  rw [← e.symm.sum_comp (fun i : α => M i i)]
  rfl

/-! ### Linear matrix maps -/

/-- Taking a submatrix is linear in the ambient matrix.

This packages the entrywise linearity of `Matrix.submatrix` in the same style
as Mathlib's block-diagonal additive and linear maps. -/
def submatrixLinearMap (R : Type*) {m n m' n' α : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α]
    (row : m' → m) (col : n' → n) :
    Matrix m n α →ₗ[R] Matrix m' n' α where
  toFun := fun A => Matrix.submatrix A row col
  map_add' := by
    intro A B
    ext i j
    rfl
  map_smul' := by
    intro c A
    ext i j
    rfl

@[simp]
theorem submatrixLinearMap_apply (R : Type*) {m n m' n' α : Type*}
    [Semiring R] [AddCommMonoid α] [Module R α]
    (row : m' → m) (col : n' → n) (A : Matrix m n α) :
    Matrix.submatrixLinearMap R row col A = Matrix.submatrix A row col :=
  rfl

/-- The trace pairing of two block-diagonal matrices is the sum of the trace
pairings of the corresponding diagonal blocks. -/
theorem trace_blockDiagonal_mul {o m R : Type*}
    [Fintype o] [DecidableEq o] [Fintype m] [NonUnitalNonAssocSemiring R]
    (B D : o → Matrix m m R) :
    Matrix.trace (Matrix.blockDiagonal B * Matrix.blockDiagonal D) =
      ∑ b : o, Matrix.trace (B b * D b) := by
  rw [← Matrix.blockDiagonal_mul B D, Matrix.trace_blockDiagonal]

end Matrix

namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-! ### Basic operator type -/

/-- Square complex matrices as the finite-dimensional operator algebra. -/
abbrev Op (d : Type*) := Matrix d d ℂ

/-! ### Kronecker product bookkeeping -/

/-- Kronecker product is additive in the right factor, rewritten for subtraction. -/
theorem kronecker_sub_right
    {d₁ d₂ : Type*} {A : Op d₁} {B₁ B₂ : Op d₂} :
    Matrix.kronecker A B₁ - Matrix.kronecker A B₂ =
      Matrix.kronecker A (B₁ - B₂) := by
  have hneg : Matrix.kronecker A (-B₂) = -Matrix.kronecker A B₂ := by
    simpa using (Matrix.kronecker_smul (-1 : ℂ) A B₂)
  calc
    Matrix.kronecker A B₁ - Matrix.kronecker A B₂
        = Matrix.kronecker A B₁ + Matrix.kronecker A (-B₂) := by
            rw [hneg]
            simp [sub_eq_add_neg]
    _ = Matrix.kronecker A (B₁ - B₂) := by
          simpa [sub_eq_add_neg] using (Matrix.kronecker_add A B₁ (-B₂)).symm

/-- Kronecker product is additive in the left factor, rewritten for subtraction. -/
theorem kronecker_sub_left
    {d₁ d₂ : Type*} {A₁ A₂ : Op d₁} {B : Op d₂} :
    Matrix.kronecker A₁ B - Matrix.kronecker A₂ B =
      Matrix.kronecker (A₁ - A₂) B := by
  have hneg : Matrix.kronecker (-A₂) B = -Matrix.kronecker A₂ B := by
    simpa using (Matrix.smul_kronecker (-1 : ℂ) A₂ B)
  calc
    Matrix.kronecker A₁ B - Matrix.kronecker A₂ B
        = Matrix.kronecker A₁ B + Matrix.kronecker (-A₂) B := by
            rw [hneg]
            simp [sub_eq_add_neg]
    _ = Matrix.kronecker (A₁ - A₂) B := by
          simpa [sub_eq_add_neg] using (Matrix.add_kronecker A₁ (-A₂) B).symm

end MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-- The equivalence between `Fin (m + n)` and `Fin (n + m)` which rotates by `n`. -/
def finAddFlip : Fin (m + n) ≃ Fin (n + m) :=
  (finSumFinEquiv.symm.trans (Equiv.sumComm _ _)).trans finSumFinEquiv

@[simp]
theorem finAddFlip_apply_castAdd (k : Fin m) (n : ℕ) :
    finAddFlip (Fin.castAdd n k) = Fin.natAdd n k := by simp [finAddFlip]

@[simp]
theorem finAddFlip_apply_natAdd (k : Fin n) (m : ℕ) :
    finAddFlip (Fin.natAdd m k) = Fin.castAdd m k := by simp [finAddFlip]

@[simp]
theorem finAddFlip_apply_mk_left {k : ℕ} (h : k < m) (hk : k < m + n := Nat.lt_add_right n h)
    (hnk : n + k < n + m := Nat.add_lt_add_left h n) :
    finAddFlip (⟨k, hk⟩ : Fin (m + n)) = ⟨n + k, hnk⟩ := by
  convert! finAddFlip_apply_castAdd ⟨k, h⟩ n

@[simp]
theorem finAddFlip_apply_mk_right {k : ℕ} (h₁ : m ≤ k) (h₂ : k < m + n) :
    finAddFlip (⟨k, h₂⟩ : Fin (m + n)) = ⟨k - m, by lia⟩ := by
  convert! @finAddFlip_apply_natAdd n ⟨k - m, by lia⟩ m
  simp [Nat.add_sub_cancel' h₁]

/-- Equivalence between `Fin m × Fin n` and `Fin (m * n)` -/
@[simps]
def finProdFinEquiv : Fin m × Fin n ≃ Fin (m * n) where
  toFun x :=
    ⟨x.2 + n * x.1,
      calc
        x.2.1 + n * x.1.1 + 1 = x.1.1 * n + x.2.1 + 1 := by ac_rfl
        _ ≤ x.1.1 * n + n := Nat.add_le_add_left x.2.2 _
        _ = (x.1.1 + 1) * n := Eq.symm <| Nat.succ_mul _ _
        _ ≤ m * n := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ x.1.2
        ⟩
  invFun x := (x.divNat, x.modNat)
  left_inv := fun ⟨x, y⟩ =>
    have H : 0 < n := Nat.pos_of_ne_zero fun H => Nat.not_lt_zero y.1 <| H ▸ y.2
    Prod.ext
      (Fin.eq_of_val_eq <|
        calc
          (y.1 + n * x.1) / n = y.1 / n + x.1 := Nat.add_mul_div_left _ _ H
          _ = 0 + x.1 := by rw [Nat.div_eq_of_lt y.2]
          _ = x.1 := Nat.zero_add x.1)
      (Fin.eq_of_val_eq <|
        calc
          (y.1 + n * x.1) % n = y.1 % n := Nat.add_mul_mod_self_left _ _ _
          _ = y.1 := Nat.mod_eq_of_lt y.2)
  right_inv _ := Fin.eq_of_val_eq <| Nat.mod_add_div _ _

import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.LowDegreePolynomial

/-!
# Finite answer spaces for the low individual degree test

Finite-type instances for the bounded polynomial answer spaces defined in
`MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.LowDegreePolynomial`.
-/

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

open scoped BigOperators

/-! ### Finite answer spaces -/

/-- The axis-line polynomial answer type uses classical equality on the bundled
polynomial witness. -/
noncomputable instance (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] :
    DecidableEq (AxisLinePolynomial params) :=
  Classical.decEq _

/-- The finite low-individual-degree polynomial answer type uses classical
equality on the bundled polynomial witness. -/
noncomputable instance (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] :
    DecidableEq (Polynomial params) :=
  Classical.decEq _

/-- A univariate polynomial of `natDegree ≤ n` is determined by its first
`n + 1` coefficients.  Shared injectivity fact behind the finite-answer-space
instances below. -/
theorem linePolynomial_coeff_fin_injective (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]
    {n : ℕ} {p q : LinePolynomialModel params}
    (hp : p.natDegree ≤ n) (hq : q.natDegree ≤ n)
    (h : ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), p.coeff i = q.coeff i) : p = q := by
  ext k
  by_cases hk : k < n + 1
  · exact h ⟨k, hk⟩
  · rw [p.coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt (hp.trans_lt (by omega)),
      q.coeff_eq_zero_of_natDegree_lt (hq.trans_lt (by omega))]

/-- Axis-line polynomial answers form a finite type via their bounded coefficient vectors. -/
noncomputable instance (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] :
    Fintype (AxisLinePolynomial params) := by
  classical
  exact Fintype.ofInjective
    (fun f : AxisLinePolynomial params => fun i : Fin (params.d + 1) => f.poly.coeff i)
    fun f g h => AxisLinePolynomial.ext
      (linePolynomial_coeff_fin_injective params f.degreeBounded g.degreeBounded
        fun i => congrFun h i)

/-- Diagonal-line polynomial answers form a finite type via their bounded coefficient vectors. -/
noncomputable instance (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] :
    Fintype (DiagonalLinePolynomial params) := by
  classical
  exact Fintype.ofInjective
    (fun f : DiagonalLinePolynomial params =>
      fun i : Fin (params.m * params.d + 1) => f.poly.coeff i)
    fun f g h => DiagonalLinePolynomial.ext
      (linePolynomial_coeff_fin_injective params f.degreeBounded g.degreeBounded
        fun i => congrFun h i)

/-- Global low-individual-degree polynomial answers form a finite type, by
injecting into the finite space of degree-restricted multivariate polynomials. -/
noncomputable instance (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q] :
    Fintype (Polynomial params) := by
  classical
  letI : Finite (MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin params.m) (Scalar params) params.d) :=
    Module.finite_of_finite (Scalar params)
  letI : Fintype (MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin params.m) (Scalar params) params.d) :=
    Fintype.ofFinite _
  exact Fintype.ofInjective
    (fun g : Polynomial params =>
      (⟨g.poly, by
          rw [MvPolynomial.mem_restrictDegree_iff_sup]
          simpa [MvPolynomial.degreeOf_def] using g.lowIndividualDegree⟩ :
        MvPolynomial.restrictDegree (Fin params.m) (Scalar params) params.d))
    fun g g' h => by
      cases g; cases g'
      simpa using congrArg Subtype.val h

/-- Reindex a polynomial-indexed sum by the value of the polynomial at a fixed point.

The low individual degree test frequently groups global polynomial answers by
the fiber of the evaluation map `h ↦ h u`.  This lemma records that finite
reindexing in the notation used throughout the LDT formalization. -/
theorem polynomial_sum_fiberwise
    (params : Parameters)
    [FieldModel params.q]
    (u : Point params)
    {β : Type*} [AddCommMonoid β]
    (f : Polynomial params → β) :
    (∑ h : Polynomial params, f h) =
      ∑ a : Fq params,
        ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : Polynomial params => h u = a), f h := by
  classical
  simpa using (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ (fun h : Polynomial params => h u) f).symm

end MIPStarRE.LDT
